sections.en: Entering Divine Service in Haste

p: בְּסִיַּעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא
With the help of Heaven.
קוּנְטְרֵס קְרָאתִיו צִדְקַת הַצַּדִּיק בִּשְׁנַת "צִדְקוֹת אָהֵב"
A pamphlet I have entitled Tzidkat HaTzadik The Righteousness of the Righteous, in the year 5662 / "He loves righteousness".
א] רֵאשִׁית כְּנִיסַת הָאָדָם לַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בְּחִפָּזוֹן,
The initial entry of a person into the service of God must be done in haste,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּפֶסַח מִצְרַיִם שֶׁהָיָה נֶאֱכָל בְּחִפָּזוֹן, וְלֹא פֶּסַח דּוֹרוֹת.
just as we find regarding the Passover of Egypt, which was eaten in haste, whereas the Passover of subsequent generations was not.
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַהַתְחָלָה לְנַתֵּק עַצְמוֹ מִכָּל תַּאֲווֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא מְקֻשָּׁר בָּהֶם,
Because at the start of tearing oneself away from all the physical desires of this world to which one is bound,
צָרִיךְ לִשְׁמֹר הָרֶגַע שֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר בּוֹ רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם,
one must seize the precise moment in which an awakening to the will of God occurs,
וְלַחְפּוֹז עַל אוֹתוֹ רֶגַע לְמַהֵר לָצֵאת מֵהֶם, אוּלַי יוּכַל.
and rush upon that very moment to hasten an escape from them, so that perhaps one may succeed.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ שׁוּב יֵלֵךְ בִּמְתִינוּת וּלְאַט, כְּדִין פֶּסַח דּוֹרוֹת.
And afterward, one may proceed with deliberation and measured patience, like the law governing the Passover of later generations.

sections.en: Blessings and Awareness of the Divine

p: ב] בְּרָכוֹת לְרֹאשׁ צַדִּיק.
"Blessings are upon the head of the righteous" (Proverbs 10:6).
לְכָךְ מַסֶּכֶת בְּרָכוֹת הַהַתְחָלָה מִשִּׁשָּׁה סְדָרִים,
For this reason, Tractate Berakhot Blessings is the opening treatise of the entire Talmud (the Six Orders),
שֶׁעִקַּר הַכֹּל: "דַּע אֶת אֱלֹהֵי אָבִיךָ" – וְאַחַר כָּךְ "וְעָבְדֵהוּ",
because the foundation of everything is: "Know the God of your father" (I Chronicles 28:9) — and only afterward, "and serve Him",
שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לֵידַע לְמִי עוֹבֵד.
for one must first know Whom one is serving.
וְזֶהוּ הַבְּרָכָה לִפְנֵי כָּל מַעֲשֶׂה, לְיַחֵד כָּל מַעֲשָׂיו לַהַשֵּׁם,
And this is the purpose of reciting a blessing before every action: to dedicate all of one's deeds to God,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "בְּכָל דְּרָכֶיךָ דָעֵהוּ", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ם רַבֵּנוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן מַיְמוֹן].
as it is written: "In all your ways acknowledge Him" (Proverbs 3:6), as Maimonides explained.
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי הַבְּרָכָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: הַשִּׁעוּר בָּהּ קָטָן שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ לְמִי מְבָרְכִין.
And this consciousness is achieved through the blessing; as the Sages stated regarding the qualifying age for a minor: a child who knows to Whom we recite blessings (Berakhot 48a).
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּשְׁאָר מִצְוֹת, אֵין הַשִּׁעוּר שֶׁיֵּדַע לְמִי מַנִּיחִין תְּפִלִּין וְכַיּוֹצֵא.
This is unlike other commandments, where the age definition is not framed around whether he knows to Whom one dons phylacteries (tefillin) or the like.
מְבֹאָר שֶׁהַבְּרָכָה עִקָּרָהּ הַיְּדִיעָה לְמִי מְבָרְכִין, שֶׁעַל כָּךְ נוֹסְדָה.
Thus it is evident that the core essence of a blessing is the awareness of Whom one addresses, for that was its foundational purpose.
וְזֶהוּ הַתְחָלַת הַכְּנִיסָה לַתּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "רֵאשִׁית חָכְמָה יִרְאַת הַשֵּׁם".
And this constitutes the primary gateway into the Torah, as it is written: "The beginning of wisdom is the fear of God" (Psalms 111:10).
וְיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם הוּא עַל יְדֵי "שִׁוִּיתִי הַשֵּׁם לְנֶגְדִּי תָמִיד", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב בַּהַגָּהָה דְּרֵישׁ אֹרַח חַיִּים.
And the fear of Heaven is attained through "I have set the Lord before me always" (Psalms 16:8), as written in the gloss of the Rema at the beginning of Shulchan Arukh, Orach Chayim.
וְהַיְנוּ בְּרָכוֹת שֶׁכֻּלָּן מַתְחִילִין בִּלְשׁוֹן נוֹכֵחַ,
This also explains why all liturgical blessings open in the second-person direct address "Blessed are You...":
שֶׁמִּיָּד בְּהַתְחָלַת הַבְּרָכָה צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹכַח עֵינָיו כְּאִלּוּ עוֹמֵד עָלָיו וּמְצַוֵּהוּ.
for at the very start of the blessing, the Blessed Name must be directly present before one's eyes, as though He is standing over him and issuing the command.
וְהַסִּיּוּם לְשׁוֹן נִסְתָּר, דְּמִיָּד נֶעְלָם,
Yet the conclusion transitions into the third person "...Who has sanctified us", because He immediately recedes into transcendence,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "עַל גּוֹזָלָיו יְרַחֵף" – נוֹגֵעַ וְאֵינוֹ נוֹגֵעַ, כַּיָּדוּעַ.
as it is written: "Over its fledglings He hovers" (Deuteronomy 32:11) — touching yet not touching, as is well known in mystical thought.

sections.en: The Yoke of Heaven by Day and Night

p: ג] עִקַּר הַקְּרִיאַת שְׁמַע: קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם וְעוֹל תּוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת, כִּדְאִיתָא (בְּרָכוֹת יג:),
The core purpose of the recitation of Shema is the acceptance of the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven and the yoke of Torah and commandments, as taught in the Talmud (Berakhot 13a),
וְצָרִיךְ בַּיּוֹם וָלַיְלָה.
and this obligation applies both by day and by night.
וְלֹא בְּבֹקֶר וָעֶרֶב, אֶלָּא "בְּשָׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ", עַיֵּן שָׁם י"א עַמּוּד א'.
Notice that the Torah did not formulate the obligation as "in the morning and evening," but rather "when you lie down and when you rise up" (cf. Berakhot 11a).
דְּיָהֵיב הַזְּמַן בָּזֶה מִשּׁוּם דְּהַבֹּקֶר וָעֶרֶב הֵם שִׁנּוּיִים בָּעוֹלָם וְלֹא בָּאָדָם,
The Torah framed the requirement in terms of human posture because morning and evening represent astronomical changes in the cosmos, not internal shifts within man;
וְהָיָה דַּי בְּקַבָּלָה אַחַת לִשְׁנֵיהֶם.
and were that the sole factor, a single daily acceptance of the yoke would have sufficed for both periods.
רַק מִפְּנֵי הַשִּׁנּוּיִים שֶׁבָּאָדָם,
Rather, it is instituted because of the practical changes taking place within the human being:
שֶׁבַּיּוֹם קָם וְעוֹסֵק בִּמְלַאכְתּוֹ, וְצָרִיךְ קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם שֶׁכָּל מַעֲשָׂיו יִהְיוּ לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם,
for during the daytime a person rises and engages in worldly work, needing the acceptance of Heaven's yoke so that all worldly labors are directed toward the service of Heaven,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֵירוּבִין סה.): "אֲנַן פּוֹעֲלֵי דִּימָמָא", כְּפוֹעֲלִים הָעוֹשִׂים מְלָאכָה שֶׁכָּל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם לָאָדוֹן,
as the Sages remarked (Eruvin 65a): "We are day-laborers," comparable to hired workers whose every effort belongs exclusively to their master,
וַאֲפִלּוּ בְּבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן מְקַצֵּר בִּשְׁבִיל עֲבוֹדָתוֹ.
such that a laborer even curtails the wording of Grace After Meals to return promptly to his employer's task.
וּבַלַּיְלָה, עֵת שְׁכִיבָה וּמְנוּחָה, צָרִיךְ גַּם כֵּן קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם,
At night, however, which is an interval of reclining and passivity, there is likewise a need to accept the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven:
שֶׁגַּם בְּשָׁכְבוֹ עַל מִטָּתוֹ יֵדַע לִפְנֵי מִי הוּא שׁוֹכֵב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב בַּהַגָּהָה דְּרֵישׁ אֹרַח חַיִּים.
so that even resting upon his bed, he remains cognizant of before Whom he is lying down, as noted in the gloss at the beginning of Orach Chayim.
וְזֶה מְלָאכָה יוֹתֵר גְּדוֹלָה.
And this internal discipline during inactivity is an even greater spiritual labor.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי בָּזֶה עַל פָּסוּק "וַיַּחֲלֹם יַעֲקֹב", שֶׁמֵּהַחֲלוֹמוֹת נִכָּר מַעֲלַת הָאָדָם,
This aligns with what I heard expounded on the verse "And Jacob dreamed" (Genesis 28:12): that a person's true stature is revealed through dreams,
אִם גַּם כְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹשֶׂה כְּלוּם, רַעְיוֹנָיו רַק "וְהִנֵּה הַשֵּׁם נִצָּב עָלָיו".
demonstrating whether even when inactive and unconscious, his thoughts remain fixated on "and behold, the Lord stood above him."
וּבְדָבָר זֶה, צַדִּיקִים מְעַטִּים שֶׁנִּתְפָּאֲרוּ כֵּן.
And in this exceptional level of devotion, only rare righteous individuals could boast such achievement.
וּלְכָךְ נָתְנוּ בְּרָכָה הַיְּתֵרָה לְעַרְבִית, שֶׁהוּא "הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ לְשָׁלוֹם".
For this reason the Sages established an additional protective blessing specifically for the evening prayer: Hashkiveinu ("Lay us down in peace").

sections.en: The Primacy of the Evening Acceptance

p: [ד] מִצְוָה רִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁנִּתְחַיֵּב הָאָדָם כְּשֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה הָאָדָם בֶּן שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה הוּא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע שֶׁל עַרְבִית, שֶׁהוּא הָרֵאשִׁית כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל,

The very first commandment a young man becomes obligated in upon reaching thirteen years of age the threshold of Bar Mitzvah at nightfall is the recitation of the evening Shema, which serves as the foundational beginning, as mentioned above.
כִּי הוּא וּבִרְכוֹת אֶחָד,
For Shema and its blessings form a single unified framework,
רַק שֶׁהַבְּרָכוֹת בִּפְרָט הַמַּעֲשִׂים, וְזוֹ בִּכְלָל עַל כָּל מַעֲשֵׂה הַקִּימָה וְעַל כָּל מַעֲשֵׂה הַשְּׁכִיבָה.
except that blessings pertain to specific, individualized actions, whereas Shema is a comprehensive acceptance governing the entire act of rising and the entire act of lying down.
וְשֶׁל עַרְבִית קוֹדֵם, כִּדְפָתַח בֵּיהּ תַּנָּא: "דִּקְרָא קָאֵי",
And the evening Shema comes first chronologically, as the Mishna opens with the evening time: "The Tanna relies on the Scriptural verse,"
וְיָלֵיף מִבְּרִיָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם לְעִנְיַן קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם:
deriving the principle from the cosmic order of Creation regarding the acceptance of the yoke of Heaven:
דִּבְרֵישָׁא חֲשׁוֹכָא,
namely, that darkness precedes light ("first there was darkness, and then there was light").
צָרִיךְ קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם אַף מִתּוֹךְ הַחֹשֶׁךְ וְהַסִּכְלוּת וְהֶעְדֵּר הַמַּעֲשִׂים,
A person must accept the yoke of Heaven's sovereignty even from within obscurity, ignorance, and the absence of spiritual deeds;
וְאָז סוֹפוֹ לְקַיְּמָהּ בְּעֹשֶׁר וּנְהוֹרָא דִּימָמָא,
and subsequently, one will merit to fulfill it amid spiritual abundance and daytime illumination—
הַשָּׂגָה הַבְּרוּרָה שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִמְשָׁךְ הַמַּעֲשֶׂה.
achieving that clear, luminous perception of the Divine through which active, tangible deeds are drawn forth into reality.

sections.en: The Sustained Continuity of the Yoke

p: ה] וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעִקַּר חִיּוּב קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם בִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע,
Although the primary obligation to accept the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven occurs during the recitation of Shema,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם חִיּוּבָהּ נִמְשָׁךְ לְעוֹלָם,
nevertheless, its obligation continues at all times,
שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ רֶגַע אֶחָד לֹא יָזוּז מִמֶּנּוּ הָעוֹל.
such that not even for a single moment should this yoke depart from him.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: "עַל חֵטְא שֶׁחָטָאנוּ לְפָנֶיךָ בִּפְרִיקַת עוֹל",
And this is like what we say in the confessional prayer: "For the sin we committed before You by casting off the yoke,"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הַבַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב עַל פָּסוּק: "אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם לֹא יַחְשֹׁב הַשֵּׁם לוֹ עָוֹן".
and as the Baal Shem Tov explained on the verse: "Praiseworthy is the person to whom the Lord imputes no iniquity" (Psalms 32:2).
וְקַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם שֶׁל עַרְבִית זְמַנָּהּ כָּל זְמַן הַשְּׁכִיבָה,
Now, the acceptance of the yoke of Heaven in the evening applies to the entire duration of lying down,
שֶׁכָּל הַלַּיְלָה צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת נוֹשֵׂא בְּעוֹל.
meaning that throughout the entire night one must carry this yoke.
אֲבָל שֶׁל שַׁחֲרִית רַק בִּתְחִלַּת הַקִּימָה,
In the morning, however, the direct obligation applies only at the initial moment of rising,
וּכְמוֹ הַבְּרָכָה בִּתְחִלַּת הַמִּצְוָה סַגִּי עַל כָּל הַמִּצְוָה, אַף שֶׁנִּמְשֶׁכֶת זְמַן מַה.
just as the blessing recited at the start of a commandment suffices for the entire duration of the mitzvah, even if it continues for a while.
לְפִי שֶׁקַּבָּלַת הָעוֹל דַּי בִּתְחִלַּת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ קְדֻשַּׁת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה מַמְשֶׁכֶת.
For accepting the yoke at the very beginning of the deed is sufficient, and thereafter the sanctity of the act carries itself forward.
וּכְמוֹ "בִּלְשְׁמָהּ" גַּבֵּי גֵּט, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב בְּתַנְיָא פֶּרֶק מ"א,
This parallels the requirement of intent "for her sake" in writing a bill of divorce, as explained in Tanya, Chapter 41;
הָכָא נַמֵּי בַּיּוֹם, שֶׁהוּא עֵת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, הוּא רַק בִּתְחִלַּת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה.
so too regarding the day, which is the time of active deed, the explicit acceptance is needed only at the inception of action.
וּכִדְדָיֵיק קְרָא "בְּשָׁכְבְּךָ" – הַיְנוּ כָּל הַלַּיְלָה דְּשׁוֹכְבִין.
And this is precise in the wording of the verse: "when you lie down" (b'shokhbekha) denotes the entire night during which one remains lying.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן "וּבְקוּמֶךָ" הוּא רַק בִּתְחִלַּת יוֹם, דְּאָז קָמִין וְעוֹמְדִין,
In contrast, "when you rise" (u'vekumekha) refers only to the start of the day, when people arise and stand up,
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן כָּל הַיּוֹם הוֹלֵךְ וְיוֹשֵׁב, וְלֹא שַׁיָּךְ "בְּקוּמֶךָ".
whereas for the rest of the day one walks and sits, so the term "when you rise" would no longer apply.
וְהַיְנוּ דְּעַל יוֹם מַעֲשֶׂה, כְּלָלוּת הַקַּבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם בִּתְחִלַּת הַיּוֹם דַּי.
This demonstrates that for an active workday, the general acceptance of the yoke of Heaven made at the outset of the day is entirely sufficient.

sections.en: The Sequential Stages of Accepting the Kingdom

p: ו] קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם שְׁלֵמָה אָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת טו.):
Regarding the complete acceptance of the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven, the Sages stated (Berakhot 15a):
"נִפְנָה" – פֵּרוּשׁ: מִכָּל גִּלּוּלֵי תַּאֲווֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַמֻּתָּרוֹת אֲשֶׁר לֹא לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם.
"He relieves himself" — meaning an inward cleansing from all the base, worldly desires, even permissible ones, that are not pursued for the sake of Heaven.
"וְנוֹטֵל יָדָיו" – שָׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁזֶּה רְמִיזַת רְחִיצַת יָדַיִם עַל סִלּוּק נְגִיעוֹת.
"And washes his hands" — I have heard from the Izbitzer Rebbe that this washing of hands is an allusion to divesting oneself of personal biases and selfish motives.
וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר עוֹד: רוֹמֵז עַל הָרְחִיצָה מִמַּה שֶּׁכְּבָר נִתְלַכְלְכוּ כְּלֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה מֵאוֹתָם הַטִּנּוּפוֹת, יִרְחָצֵם בְּמֵי הַדַּעַת וְטָהֵר.

And one could further suggest: it hints at washing clean the instruments of action that were soiled by those base contaminations, cleansing them in the purifying waters of divine understanding so that one becomes pure.
"וּמַנִּיחַ תְּפִלִּין" – כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב בְּיַעֲרוֹת דְּבַשׁ, שֶׁהוּא חוֹתַם שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם שֶׁנּוֹשֵׂא עָלָיו,
"And dons phylacteries" — as written in Ya'arot Devash, this is the seal of Heaven's Name that one bears upon oneself,
כְּמוֹ עֶבֶד שֶׁנּוֹשֵׂא הַנִּשְׁקָא מֵאֲדוֹנוֹ לְאוֹת שֶׁהוּא אֲדוֹנוֹ.
like a servant who wears the badge or insignia of his master to signify who his master is:
וְעַל יָדוֹ לְאוֹת לְעַצְמוֹ, וְעַל הָרֹאשׁ לְאוֹת לְכָל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ כִּי שְׁמָא דְּמָרֵיהּ עֲלֵיהּ.
upon his arm as an internal sign to himself, and upon the head as a visible sign to all peoples of the earth that the Name of the Master is upon him.
"וְקוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע" – קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם וְעוֹל תּוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת.
"And recites Shema" — which is the explicit acceptance of the yoke of Heaven and the yoke of Torah and commandments.
"וּמִתְפַּלֵּל" – גַּם זֶה מִכְּלַל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ תּוֹסָפוֹת יד ב].
"And prays" — and this too falls under the category of accepting the Kingdom of Heaven, as Tosafot note on 14b.
כִּי קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע אֵינוֹ לְנֹכַח הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן תְּפִלָּה, כִּדְפֵירֵשׁ רַשִׁ"י (בְּרָכוֹת כה רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א),
For Shema is not recited in direct personal encounter facing the Blessed Name, whereas the Amidah prayer is, as Rashi explains (Berakhot 25a);
וּשְׁלֵמוּת הַמַּלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לְנֹכַח הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
and the full perfection of accepting Heaven's kingdom is achieved when standing face-to-face before the Blessed Name.
וְאַחַר כָּל הַהֲכָנוֹת אֵלּוּ, אָז מִתְפַּלֵּל.
And only following all of these sequential preparations does one then engage in prayer.

sections.en: The Spiritual Significance of Meal Times and Shema

p: ז] זְמַן קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע תָּלֵי בִּזְמַן אֲכִילָה בַּמִּשְׁנָה דְּרֵישׁ בְּרָכוֹת, וְשָׁם בַּבָּרַיְתָא עַמּוּד ב'.
The time established for reciting Shema is tethered to meal times in the opening Mishna of Berakhot, and in the Baraita on 2b.
כִּי אֲכִילָה הוּא קִיּוּם הַחַיִּים, וְכָךְ קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם.
For eating sustains physical life, and similarly, the acceptance of the yoke of Heaven sustains spiritual life.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאֲכִילַת הָאָדָם בַּבֹּקֶר וּבָעֶרֶב, כָּךְ קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם.
And just as a person eats in the morning and in the evening, so too must one accept the yoke of Heaven morning and evening.
וּמַאן דְּאָמַר: מֵעָנִי – בְּדַעַת, שֶׁאֵין לוֹ נֵר לְהָאִיר עֵינֵי שִׂכְלוֹ וּמְמַהֵר בַּאֲכִילָה פְּשׁוּטָה,

The authority who measures this time by "when a poor man eats" refers allegorically to one poor in spiritual knowledge, who lacks a candle to illuminate his intellectual vision and quickly partakes of simple fare;
כָּךְ קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם בִּפְשִׁיטוּת כְּעָנִי זֶה שֶׁאוֹכֵל רַק פַּת בְּמֶלַח.
so too his acceptance of Heaven's yoke is simple and plain, like this poor man who eats merely bread with salt.
וְחַד מַאן דְּאָמַר: דְּבָתַר רוֹב בְּנֵי אָדָם, דְּגַם כֵּן אֵין צָרִיךְ טָהֳרָה,
Another authority holds that the time follows the majority of people, who likewise require no ritual purity,
רַק מְתִינוּת קְצָת עַד שֶׁיִּהְיֶה "נֵר הַשֵּׁם נִשְׁמַת אָדָם" מֵאִיר עֵינֵי שִׂכְלָם.
requiring merely a bit of composure until "the lamp of the Lord, which is the soul of man" illuminates the eyes of their mind.
וּלְחַד מַאן דְּאָמַר: כִּבְלֵילֵי שַׁבָּת, שֶׁהַכֹּל מוּכָן מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם,
And according to the opinion comparing it to Friday evening, when everything has been prepared before nightfall:
וְדַי לִקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע שֶׁל עַרְבִית הַהַכָנָה שֶׁמִּבְּעוֹד יוֹם עַל יְדֵי מַעֲשֵׂה הַיּוֹם, וְאֵין צָרִיךְ הַכָנָה אַחֶרֶת.
the preparation made before sunset through the day's active deeds is sufficient for the evening Shema, with no further preparation needed.
וְהַהֲלָכָה כַּכֹּהֲנִים, שֶׁהֵם הַבַּטְלָנִים מִכָּל עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם אֶלָּא עֵסֶק הַתּוֹרָה,
Yet the halakhic ruling follows the priests (Kohanim), who are detached from all mundane matters of this world, engaged solely in Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ם רַבֵּנוּ מֹשֶׁה בֶּן מַיְמוֹן] סוֹף הִלְכוֹת שְׁמִטָּה וְיוֹבֵל, וְכֵן שָׁמַעְתִּי בָּזֶה,
as Maimonides wrote at the end of the Laws of Shemittah and Yovel, and as I have likewise heard on this subject.
וַאֲכִילָתָם קֹדֶשׁ לַהַשֵּׁם וּצְרִיכִים טָהֳרָה,
Their eating is holy unto God and requires ritual purification;
וְכָךְ לִקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע: נִפְנֶה וְנוֹטֵל יָדָיו קֹדֶם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל פֵּרוּשׁוֹ.
and so it is for Shema: one first relieves himself and washes his hands, corresponding to the deeper meaning explained above.

sections.en: Preparation, Prayer Windows, and the Obscurity of Night

p: ח] וּזְמַן הַהַכָנָה הַזּוֹ הַכֹּל לְפִי מַה שֶּׁהוּא אָדָם,
The duration required for this preparation depends entirely on the spiritual standing of each individual person,
וַחֲסִידִים הָיוּ שׁוֹהִים רַק שָׁעָה אַחַת לִתְפִלָּה, כִּדְאִיתָא (בְּרָכוֹת ל:).
and early pious men (Chassidim) would tarry for one hour in preparation for prayer, as taught in the Talmud (Berakhot 30b).
וְזֶה טַעַם גַּם כֵּן שֶׁהִרְחִיבוּ בִּזְמַן שֶׁל עַרְבִית עַד עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר,
This also explains why the Rabbis extended the permissible timeframe for the evening prayer until the break of dawn:
כִּי בְּחֶשְׁכַת לַיִל קָשֶׁה לִמְצֹא בְּהִירוּת מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם, פְּעָמִים עַד עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר כּוּלֵּי הַאי וְאוּלַי.
because in the deep obscurity of night it is hard to attain the luminous clarity of Heaven's kingdom, and at times even taking until dawn is scarcely enough.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּיּוֹם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "לְהַגִּיד בַּבֹּקֶר חַסְדֶּךָ" – אָז אֶפְשָׁר לְהַגִּיד מִיָּד בַּבֹּקֶר מִתּוֹךְ אוֹר הַנִּכָּר.
By day, however, as it is written: "To recount Your lovingkindness in the morning" (Psalms 92:3), one can readily proclaim it right away in the morning amidst visible light.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּלֵּילוֹת, רַק הָאֱמוּנָה בַּלֵּב וְלֹא הַהַגָּדָה, שֶׁהוּא הַהוֹצָאָה מִכֹּחַ אֶל הַפּוֹעַל עַל הֶעָבָר,
In the night, by contrast, there is only inner faith in the heart without vocal recounting—for recounting brings past reality into dynamic actuality—
אֶלָּא הַקִּוּוּי עַל הֶעָתִיד כַּאֲשֶׁר "אָתָא בֹקֶר", גַּם בְּכָל הַלַּיְלָה כֻּלָּהּ.
and instead one can only express yearning for the future, for when "morning comes," persisting through the entire night.
וּלְכָךְ תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית רְשׁוּת,
For this reason, the evening prayer was originally categorized as optional (reshut),
כִּי תְּפִלָּה הוּא הַכָּרַת הַנֹּכַח יוֹתֵר מִקְּרִיאַת שְׁמַע, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל אוֹת ו',
because prayer requires facing God directly even more than Shema does (as I wrote above in Section 6),
וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְחַיֵּב בַּלַּיְלָה, דְּ"זֶה שְּׁמִי לְעֹלָם" כְּתִיב, בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁדּוֹמֶה לְלַיְלָה.
and one cannot impose such direct obligation at night, for it is written: "This is My Name to be concealed" (le'alem) in this world, which resembles night.
רַק רְשׁוּת לְמִי שֶׁחֲנָנוֹ הַשֵּׁם לִהְיוֹת "לַיְלָה כַּיּוֹם יָאִיר" לוֹ.
It remained optional for someone whom God granted the favor that "night shines for him like the day."
רַק הָאִידְּנָא, בְּעִקְּבוֹת דִּמְשִׁיחָא, קָרוֹב לְאוֹר הַיּוֹם, קִבְּלִינְהוּ לְחוֹבָה.
Only in our later era, amidst the footsteps of the Messiah when the light of day draws near, did Jewish communities accept it as an absolute obligation.
וּתְפִלַּת הַשַּׁחַר גַּם כֵּן זְמַנָּהּ עַד חֲצוֹת, יוֹתֵר מִזְּמַן קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע,
Similarly, the morning prayer may be recited until midday—extending beyond the timeframe for the morning Shema—
כִּי לְקַבָּלַת הַנֹּכַח מִמַּלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם צָרִיךְ הַכָנָה יוֹתֵר.
because achieving the face-to-face consciousness of Heaven's kingdom demands greater preparation.
וּלְכָךְ יֵשׁ תַּשְׁלוּמִין לִתְפִלָּה אֵצֶל תְּפִלָּה הַסְּמוּכָה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעָבַר הַזְּמַן.
And for this reason, missed prayers can be made up during the immediately following prayer even though the original time has passed;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּתְּפִלָּה הַשְּׁלִישִׁית הָוֵי "מְעֻוָּת לֹא יוּכַל לִתְקֹן]", כוּלֵי,
whereas skipping two prayers makes it "a crooked thing that cannot be made straight,"
דִּבְתְרֵי זִמְנֵי הָוֵי חֲזָקָה לְגַבֵּי אוֹתָהּ דְּלָא מָצֵי מְכַוֵּין לָהּ.
for missing twice creates a presumption of spiritual incapacity regarding concentrating properly on that missing prayer.

sections.en: The Gravity of Passive Omission

p: ט] יָשַׁב אָדָם וְלֹא עָשָׂה מִצְוָה שֶׁחוֹבָה עָלָיו לַעֲשׂוֹתָהּ – כְּאִלּוּ עָשָׂה עֲבֵרָה.
If a person sits idly and fails to perform a commandment he is obligated to do, it is considered as though he committed an active transgression.
כָּךְ שָׁמַעְתִּי מִדִּיּוּק לְשׁוֹן הַמִּשְׁנָה דְּרֵישׁ בְּרָכוֹת: "לְהַרְחִיק מִן הָעֲבֵרָה".
Thus I heard derived from the precise wording of the opening Mishna of Berakhot: "in order to distance man from transgression."
וּפָשׁוּט הוּא, שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יז.):
And this concept is straightforward, for we find similarly (Rosh Hashanah 17a):
"פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּגוּפָן – קַרְקַפְתָּא דְּלָא מַנַּח תְּפִלִּין",
"The transgressors of Israel with their bodies are defined as a skull that does not put on tefillin,"
אַף עַל גַּב דְּאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בְּ"שֵׁב וְאַל תַּעֲשֶׂה".
even though this omission is merely passive inaction ("sit and do nothing").

sections.en: Anchoring Study in the Divine Word

p: י] כָּל בִּנְיַן לִמּוּדוֹ יִהְיֶה עַל הַמִּקְרָא שֶׁצִּוָּה הַשֵּׁם,
The entire edifice of a person's Torah study must be anchored upon the Scripture that God commanded,
וְזֶה יִהְיֶה נֹכַח עֵינָיו, כִּי עַל זֶה הוּא דָּן: עַל מַה שֶּׁצִּוָּה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּתוֹרָתוֹ.
and this must remain constantly before his eyes, for this is what he is analyzing: that which the Blessed Name commanded in His Torah.
וְעַל זֶה רָמַז בְּרֹאשׁ הַמִּשְׁנָיוֹת, דְּפָתַח: "מֵאֵימָתַי", וְתַנָּא אַקְּרָא קָאֵי, כִּדִמְפָרֵשׁ בַּגְּמָרָא.
And the Sages hinted at this at the very beginning of the Mishnayot, opening with "From when...", where the Talmud clarifies that the Tanna stands anchored upon Scripture.
לְאוֹרוֹיֵי דְּכָל מִשְׁנָתוֹ רַק אַקְּרָא קָאֵי,
This teaches that his entire teaching is founded strictly on the Biblical text,
וְלֹא כְּלִמּוּד חָכְמָה מֵחָכְמוֹת.
and not like the study of standard secular disciplines and philosophies.
וְכִמְדֻמֶּה שֶׁכָּךְ שָׁמַעְתִּי גַּם כֵּן.
And I believe I heard this precise concept taught as well.

sections.en: We Learn from the Creation of the World That in All Matters the Night…

p: יא] יָלְפִינַן מִבְּרִיָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם דִּבְכָל דָּבָר הַלַּיְלָה קוֹדֵם לַיּוֹם כִּדְאִיתָא רֵישׁ בְּרָכוֹת.
We learn from the creation of the world that in all matters the night precedes the day, as taught at the beginning of Berakhot (2a).
כִּי בְכָל דָּבָר הַהֶעְדֵּר קוֹדֵם לַהֲוָיָה,
For in everything, absence precedes existence;
וְ"כִי אֵשֵׁב בַּחֹשֶׁךְ" אֵדַע כִּי אַחַר כָּךְ "ה' אוֹר לִי".
and "when I sit in darkness," I know that afterward "Hashem will be a light unto me" (Micah 7:8).
כִּי כָל חַיֵּי הָאָדָם כָּךְ מוּרְכָּבִים מֵהַזְּמַן: חֹשֶׁךְ וְאוֹר, יוֹם וָלַיְלָה, כָּךְ חוֹזֵר חָלִילָה,
For a person's entire life is thus compounded of time: darkness and light, day and night, cycling repeatedly;
רַק שֶׁהַחֹשֶׁךְ קוֹדֵם, דִּקְלִיפָּה קוֹדֶמֶת לַפְּרִי.
only that darkness comes first, just as the peel precedes the fruit.
חוּץ בְּקָדָשִׁים קַיְימָא לַן: הַלַּיְלָה אַחַר הַיּוֹם,
This applies universally except regarding sacrificial holy offerings (kodashim), where we maintain that night follows day;
כִּי מִי שֶׁכְּבָר בָּא אֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ הַיּוֹם קוֹדֵם, כְּמוֹ מִי שֶׁעוֹמֵד תּוֹךְ הַפְּרִי אֶצְלוֹ הַפְּרִי קוֹדֵם לַקְּלִיפָּה
for one who has already entered the realm of holiness has day first, like one standing inside the fruit for whom the fruit precedes the peel
וּלְכָךְ סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ גַּם לִקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר].
and therefore one might initially have thought this should apply to the recitation of Shema as well, as I wrote elsewhere.
וְעַיֵּין בְּתַלְמִידֵי רַבֵּנוּ יוֹנָה בְּרָכוֹת ח' עַמּוּד א' דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "וְאוֹמֵר", דְּגַם בַּתּוֹרָה כֵּן.
And see Talmidei Rabbeinu Yonah on Berakhot 8a (s.v. Ve-omer), showing that in Torah study it is likewise so.

sections.en: Regarding Repentance, There Are Two Facets

p: יב] בִּתְשׁוּבָה יֵשׁ שְׁנֵי עִנְיָנִים: לְהַבָּא וְתִיקּוּן הֶעָבָר,
Regarding repentance, there are two facets: orientation for the future, and rectification of the past;
וְזֶהוּ טַעֲמָא שֶׁצָּרִיךְ שְׁנֵי דְבָרִים: טָהֳרָה עַל לְהַבָּא
and this is the reason why two elements are required: purification for the future

[בְּמֵי הַדַּעַת הוּא תּוֹרָה תַּבְלִין וּמַצְלֵי מֵעֲבֵירוֹת לְהַבָּא שֶׁהַמָּאוֹר מַחֲזִיר לְמוּטָב כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּמִּדְרָשׁ רֵישׁ אֵיכָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כה) שֶׁהַתְּשׁוּבָה: לָמַד דַּף אֶחָד יִלְמוֹד שְׁנֵי דַפִּים]

through the waters of divine understanding, which is Torah serving as the antidote saving from future sin, since its inner illumination restores one to good, as stated in the Midrash at the beginning of Eichah, and as taught in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu and Vayikra Rabbah 25:1, that repentance requires: 'if he was accustomed to study one page, let him now study two pages',
וְכַפָּרָה הוּא לְתַקֵּן הֶעָבָר וּלְכַפֵּר הַחֵטְא,
and atonement (kapparah) to repair the past and atone for sin,
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי קָרְבָּן וְדוּגְמָתוֹ תְּפִלָּה אוֹ תַּעֲנִית וּצְדָקָה.
which is accomplished through sacrifice, and in its absence through prayer, fasting, and charity.
וְקַיְימָא לַן כַּפָּרָה לֹא מְעַכֶּבֶת, דִּתְשׁוּבָה אֲפִילּוּ הִרְהֵר בְּלִבּוֹ הֲרֵי זֶה צַדִּיק גָּמוּר,

And we establish the halakhic rule that the lack of final atonement does not impede spiritual status, for regarding repentance, even if one merely resolved so in his heart, he is immediately deemed completely righteous;
וְזֶהוּ רַק לִתְרוּמָה הַמּוּרָם מִן הַחוֹל הַגָּמוּר לִהְיוֹת עַל כָּל פָּנִים בְּגֶדֶר צַדִּיק.
yet this level of partial purification suffices only for terumah (the priestly tithe), being elevated from pure mundane commonality so as to enter at least the category of righteous.
אֲבָל לְקָדָשִׁים הָרוֹצֶה לְהִתְקַדֵּשׁ וְלִהְיוֹת קָדוֹשׁ צָרִיךְ גַּם כֵּן לְרַפֵּא אֶת הַקּוֹדֵם.
But for sacred offerings (kodashim), one who desires to become sanctified and holy must also thoroughly heal all that preceded.
וְתָלֵי זְמַן קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם בִּתְרוּמָה, דְּכַפָּרָה לֹא מְעַכֵּב לְקַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם וּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע דְּהַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה,

And the timeframe for accepting the yoke of Heaven is linked specifically to terumah, because the lack of past atonement does not bar the acceptance of the yoke of Heaven and the recitation of Shema, which is Torah study;
כָּךְ פֵּירֵשׁ רַשִּׁ"י שָׁם רֵישׁ בְּרָכוֹת בְּשֵׁם הַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי וּבִמְנָחוֹת צ"ט עַמּוּד ב' עַיֵּין שָׁם.
thus Rashi explains at the beginning of Berakhot citing the Yerushalmi, and in Menachot 99b, see there.
"וְלָרָשָׁע אָמַר אֱלֹהִים מַה לְּךָ לְסַפֵּר חֻקָּי",
Scripturally, "unto the wicked God said: What right have you to recount My statutes?" (Psalms 50:16);
אֲבָל מִיָּד שֶׁנִּטְהַר עַל לְהַבָּא הֲרֵי זֶה צַדִּיק גָּמוּר וְיָכוֹל לְקַבֵּל עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם.
but the moment a person resolves upon purity for the future, he is instantly fully righteous and qualified to accept the yoke of Heaven.
רַק הַעֲרֵב שֶׁמֶשׁ צָרִיךְ, דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁעָבַר יוֹמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה טָמֵא וְהֶעֱרִיב עָלָיו הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ בְּטָהֳרָה,
He requires only the setting of the sun (ha'arev shemesh), meaning that the day in which he was defiled must pass and the sun must set upon him in a state of purity;
וְזֶהוּ שִׁינּוּי זְמַן עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ם (פֶּרֶק ב מֵהִלְכוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה) בְּשִׁינּוּי הַשֵּׁם, כִּלְשׁוֹנוֹ: אֵינִי עוֹמֵד עַכְשָׁו בְּאוֹתוֹ זְמַן וּגְבוּל כָּעֵת שֶׁנִּטְמֵאתִי,

and this temporal shift operates like the principle explained by Maimonides (Hilkhot Teshuvah 2:4) regarding changing one's name, as if to say: "I no longer stand within the same time and boundary as when I became defiled,"
כִּי הַהוּא יוֹמָא דְּקָא גָּרִים, שֶׁבְּכָל יוֹם הָאָדָם עוֹמֵד בְּעִנְיָן אַחֵר.
for that elapsed day caused the transition, since with each new day a person stands in an entirely refreshed state.
וְשִׁמְשָׁא מִמֵּילָא עָרְבָא עַל יְדֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, כִּי אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ וְכוּלֵי:
And the sun sets on its own by the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, for without the Holy One assisting him, man could never prevail.

sections.en: Time Is Composed of Day and Night

p: יג] הַזְּמַן מוּרְכָּב מִיּוֹם וָלַיְלָה וְכֵן חַיֵּי הָאָדָם אוֹר וְחֹשֶׁךְ עוֹלֶה וְיוֹרֵד,
Time is composed of day and night, and so too is human life: light and darkness, ascending and descending,
כִּידוּעַ מַאֲמַר הַבַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב עַל פָּסוּק "שֶׁבַע יִפּוֹל צַדִּיק וָקָם".
as is known from the Baal Shem Tov's teaching on the verse: "Seven times does the righteous fall and rise up" (Proverbs 24:16).
כִּי שִׁבְעָה יָמִים הוּא שָׁבוּעַ אֶחָד וְאַחַר כָּךְ חוֹזְרִים אוֹתָן שִׁבְעָה יָמִים חָלִילָה.
For seven days constitute one week, and thereafter those same seven days recur in cycle.
וְאָמְנָם גַּם בְּעֵת הַחֹשֶׁךְ צָרִיךְ אוֹר הַלְּבָנָה אוֹ אוֹר כּוֹכָבִים דְּנַמֵּי אוֹר הוּא כִּדְאִיתָא רֵישׁ פְּסָחִים, וְלֹא שֶׁיְּהֵא חָשׁוּךְ לְגַמְרֵי.
Indeed, even during the period of darkness one needs the light of the moon or the stars, which is also recognized as light (Pesachim 2a), so that it not be total obscurity.
וּבְבֵיתוֹ צָרִיךְ אוֹר הַנֵּר
And inside one's house, one requires the light of a candle

[מִצְוָה, וְאוֹר תּוֹרָה "שֶׁמֶשׁ וּמָגֵן ה'", זֶהוּ תּוֹרָה לִשְׁמָהּ בִּבְהִירוּת הַכָּרַת שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, וְזֶהוּ "וְאֹהֲבָיו כְּצֵאת הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ", וּ"מַצְדִּיקֵי הָרַבִּים כַּכּוֹכָבִים" שֶׁלּוֹמְדִים תּוֹרָה נִגְלֶה לָרַבִּים].

a mitzvah; and the light of Torah is as 'the sun and shield of Hashem,' namely Torah studied for its own sake in radiant awareness of Heaven; and this is 'those who love Him are like the sun rising in its strength' (Judges 5:31), while 'those who turn many to righteousness are like the stars' (Daniel 12:3), teaching manifest Torah publicly.
וּפֵירוּשׁ "בְּבֵיתוֹ" – בְּחַדְרֵי לְבָבוֹ, אוֹר הַנֵּר יָפֶה לִבְדִיקָה,
And 'inside his house' means within the inner chambers of his heart, where candlelight is ideal for inspection:
שְׁאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה הַטָּמוּן בְּחוֹרִין וּבִסְדָקִין זֶה טוֹב יוֹתֵר בַּלַּיְלָה בְּעֵת הַחֹשֶׁךְ שֶׁאָז אוֹר הַנֵּר מֵאִיר
searching out the leaven in the dough hidden within holes and cracks is accomplished far better at night during darkness, when candlelight shines brightly

[מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּיּוֹם אֵין מֵאִיר דִּשְׁרָגָא בְּטִיהֲרָא, וְעַיֵּין בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי רֵישׁ פְּסָחִים דִּבְיוֹם אַף בְּמָקוֹם חָשׁוּךְ אֵין מֵאִיר כָּל כָּךְ, בִּזְמַן שֶׁשֵּׁם שָׁמַיִם נִגְלֶה עַל כָּל פְּנֵי הָעוֹלָם קָטָן אֵין נֵר מִצְוָה חָשׁוּב לִכְלוּם],

unlike daytime when a lamp in broad daylight yields no benefit (Chullin 60b), and see Yerushalmi Pesachim 1:1 that by day even in a dark chamber a candle does not illuminate well; for when the Divine Name is fully manifest over the micro-cosmos, the candle of an isolated mitzvah is eclipsed,
וְעַל יָדוֹ יָכוֹל לִבְדּוֹק כָּל הַמִּינֵי חִימּוּץ מִסִּדְקֵי לְבָבוֹ עַד מָקוֹם שֶׁיָּדוֹ מַגַּעַת, וְהַשְּׁאָר מְבַטְּלוֹ בְּלִבּוֹ.
and through this inspection one can purge all subtle souring impurities from the crevices of the heart as far as human reach extends, nullifying whatever remains in his heart.
וְהִנֵּה אוֹר הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ מְטַהֵר זְמַן הַיּוֹם, וְהַשְׁלָמַת הַטָּהֳרָה כַּאֲשֶׁר אִיעֲרַב שִׁמְשָׁא כִּדְאִיתָא בְּרָכוֹת ב',
And behold, sunlight purifies the hours of the day, with complete purity finalized once the sun sets (Berakhot 2b);
דְּלוּלֵי נִטְהַר לֹא אִיעֲרַב עֲדַיִן, וְכָל כַּמָּה דְּלָא אִיעֲרַב עֲדַיִן צָרִיךְ אוֹתוֹ זְמַן טָהֳרָה עַל יְדֵי אוֹר הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ שֶׁהוּא מִשְׁתַּדֵּל בְּטָהֳרָתוֹ:

for had he not immersed for purity the sun would not set effectively upon him, and so long as it has not set he still requires that interval of purification under sunlight while exerting himself toward total purity.

sections.en: Even During the Day There Are Times When Clouds Obstruct Direct Light Without Bringing…

p: יד] וְגַם בַּיּוֹם יֵשׁ פְּעָמִים עֲנָנִים הַמּוֹנְעִים הָאוֹר אֲבָל לֹא מַחְשִׁיכִים.
Even during the day there are times when clouds obstruct direct light without bringing darkness.
וְהֵם לְטוֹבָה, כִּי הַמִּסְתַּכֵּל בַּשֶּׁמֶשׁ עֵינָיו כֵּהוֹת, וְגַם לִמְנוֹעַ תּוֹקֶף הַחֹם הַמַּזִּיק פְּעָמִים לָאָדָם כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּנָדָב וַאֲבִיהוּא.
And these clouds are beneficial, for one who gazes directly into the sun dims his vision, and they temper intense heat that can harm a person, as found with Nadav and Avihu.
וְגַם עִיקַּר טוֹבָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי בְּעִנְיָן זֶה עַל פָּסוּק "הַמְכַסֶּה שָׁמַיִם בְּעָבִים הַמֵּכִין לָאָרֶץ מָטָר",
Moreover, they bring essential goodness, as I heard on the verse "Who covers the heavens with clouds, Who prepares rain for the earth" (Psalms 147:8):
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה מוֹרִיד טִיפָּה חֲדָשָׁה לַגּוּף הַמַּצְמַחַת, אֲבָל הַמָּטָר עַצְמוֹ אֵינוֹ טוֹבָה אֶלָּא בִּזְמַנּוֹ.
through clouds a fresh revitalizing drop descends upon the body to cause growth, though rain is beneficial only in its proper season.

וּפְעָמִים שֶׁהֶעָנָן רָעָה שֶׁצָּרִיךְ תּוֹקֶף הַחֹם, וְהוּא בְּעֵת גְּמַר הַקְּצִירָה שֶׁהוּא גְּמַר הַמַּעֲשֶׂה דִּמְכוּנֶּה קְצִירָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסוֹף פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּבָבָא קַמָּא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר:

Conversely, at times a cloud is detrimental when the full intensity of heat is necessary, such as the culmination of the harvest representing the final stage of practical accomplishment, as taught at the end of the first chapter of Bava Kamma and as I noted elsewhere.

sections.en: A Mitzvah Is a Spiritual Privilege When It Presents Itself to a Person

p: טו] מִצְוָה הוּא זְכוּת לָאָדָם שֶׁתִּזְדַּמֵּן לְיָדוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "שְׂכַר מִצְוָה – מִצְוָה",
A mitzvah is a spiritual privilege when it presents itself to a person, as stated: "the reward of a mitzvah is a mitzvah" (Avot 4:2),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹסֶפְתָּא (פֵּאָה פֶּרֶק ג) בְּאוֹתוֹ שֶׁנִּזְדַּמְּנָה לְיָדוֹ מִצְוַת שִׁכְחָה הֵבִיא עוֹלָה,
and as related in the Tosefta (Peah 3:8) concerning the man who happened to fulfill the forgotten sheaf (shikhchah) and brought a burnt offering in thanksgiving,
וּבְסֻכָּה (כח:) דִּגְשָׁמִים בֶּחָג סִימָן רַע מָשָׁל וְכוּלֵי,
and in Sukkah (28b) that rain on Sukkot is an unfavorable omen, comparable to a servant whose master pours the ladle back in his face,
וּבְחוֹבוֹת הַלְּבָבוֹת: כַּאֲשֶׁר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רוֹצֶה לִשְׁלוֹחַ דּוֹרוֹן לְאוֹהֲבוֹ מַזְמִין לוֹ עָנִי.
and in Chovot HaLevavot: when the Blessed Name wishes to send a gift to His beloved, He sends him a poor person.
וְלָכֵן מְבָרְכִין "שֶׁהֶחֱיָנוּ" עַל מִצְווֹת שֶׁקְּבוּעַ זְמַן.
For this reason we recite the Shehecheyanu blessing over commandments tied to specific designated times.
וְזֶהוּ הַלָּשׁוֹן "זַכָּאִין לֶאֱכוֹל בִּתְרוּמָה" בִּבְרָכוֹת ב' עַמּוּד ב', דַּאֲכִילַת תְּרוּמָה מִצְוָה כִּדְאִיתָא פְּסָחִים (עג רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א).
And this explains the Talmudic phrasing "entitled (zakka'in, rooted in zekhut / merit) to eat of terumah" in Berakhot 2b, for eating terumah is itself a mitzvah (Pesachim 73a).
וְתַנָּא דִידַן: "נִכְנָסִין", לְאוֹרוֹיֵי דְּכֹהֲנִים זְרִיזִים וּזְרִיזִים מַקְדִּימִין,
Our Tanna uses the term "enter" (nikhnasin) to teach that priests are zealous and the zealous act early:
וְתֵיכֶף בְּרֶגַע רִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁמְּטוֹהָרִים הֵם נִכְנָסִים, שֶׁמִּיָּד בְּהַגִּיעַ זְמַן הַמִּצְוָה יַתְחִיל הַכְּנִיסָה וְהַהַכָנָה לַמִּצְוָה.
at the very first moment they are purified they enter, teaching that the instant a mitzvah's time arrives, one must begin the entrance and preparation for it.
וַאֲגַב אוֹרְחָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּצָרִיךְ כְּנִיסָה וְהַכָנָה לַמִּצְוָה וְלֹא אוֹכְלִין מִיָּד.
Incidendal to this, we learn that every mitzvah requires entrance and preparation, rather than eating immediately.
וּמַאן דְּאָמַר "מְטוֹהָרִין", יֵשׁ לוֹמַר דְּתוֹסָפוֹת דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "מִשָּׁעָה" הִקְשׁוּ עַיֵּין שָׁם,
And for the authority who says "purified" (metoharin), one can address the difficulty raised by Tosafot (s.v. Mishe'ah, see there):
וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר "נִכְנָס" הַיְינוּ הַכָנָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל וּבִשְׁעַת כְּנִיסָה יִקְרָא,
"entering" denotes preparatory entry, during which one recites Shema;
וְהַאי מַאן דְּאָמַר סוֹבֵר דְּאֵין פְּנַאי בִּשְׁעַת כְּנִיסָה לְקַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם וּתְפִלָּה, דְּדַי בְּהַכָנָה מוּעֶטֶת.
and that authority holds there is no leisure during entry for accepting Heaven's yoke and prayer, a brief preparation being sufficient.
אִי נַמֵּי סוֹבֵר דְּקַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם אֵינוֹ רָאוּי בִּשְׁעַת כְּנִיסָה דְּאֵינוֹ מֵעִנְיַן הַהַכָנָה רַק מִצְוָה בְּאַפֵּי נַפְשָׁהּ, לְכָךְ אָמַר "מְטוֹהָרִין".
Alternatively, he holds that accepting the yoke of Heaven is unsuitable during entry, not being an intrinsic preparatory step but an independent mitzvah, which is why he formulated it as "purified."
וְתַנָּא דִידַן דְּקַיְימָא לַן כְּוָותֵיהּ סָבַר דְּקַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם וּתְפִלָּה הוּא עַצְמוֹ הַהַכָנָה וּמֵעִנְיָנָהּ,
But our Tanna, whose opinion is halakhically authoritative, holds that accepting the yoke of Heaven and praying is itself the essential preparation;
וְהַכָנָה כָּזוֹ צָרִיךְ לִפְנֵי הַמִּצְווֹת: שֶׁיְּקַבֵּל עָלָיו קוֹדֶם עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם בְּנִסְתָּר דְּהַיְינוּ קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע, וּבְנוֹכַח שֶׁהוּא תְּפִלָּה.
and such preparation is required prior to commandments: accepting Heaven's yoke in the third person (nistar) through Shema, and in the direct second person (nokhe'ach) through prayer.
וְזֶהוּ הַבְּרָכָה שֶׁלִּפְנֵי אֲכִילָה שֶׁהוּא נוֹכַח וְנִסְתָּר,
This mirrors the blessing recited before eating, which transitions from second-person presence to third-person transcendence;
וּמַתְחֶלֶת בְּנוֹכַח, שֶׁגַּם לִבְרָכָה צָרִיךְ הַכָנָה שֶׁגַּם הוּא נַעֲשָׂה מִצְוָה דְּרַבָּנָן כֵּיוָן שֶׁיּוֹצֵא לַפּוֹעַל בְּדִבּוּר.
opening in direct address to show that even a blessing requires preparation, having become a rabbinic precept expressed through tangible speech.
וְעוֹד עַיֵּין מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי בָּזֶה בְּקוּנְטְרֵס "עֵת הָאֹכֶל".
And see further what I wrote on this in my treatise Et HaOchel.

sections.en: A Mitzvah Performed on Account of Doubt Certainly Bears the Holiness of the Blessed…

p: [טז] דְּבַר מִצְוָה שֶׁעוֹשֵׂהוּ מִפְּנֵי הַסָּפֵק חָל עָלָיו קְדוּשַׁת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּוַדַּאי כֵּיוָן שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹתוֹ מִפְּנֵי הַסָּפֵק, דּוּגְמַת יוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי.

A mitzvah performed on account of doubt certainly bears the holiness of the Blessed Name, since fulfilling it out of doubt is an established obligation, exemplified by the second festival day of the Diaspora (Yom Tov Sheni).

וְעַיֵּין שַׁבָּת כ"ג עַמּוּד א' דִּמְבָרְכִין "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו" אַסָּפֵק, חוּץ מִדְּמַאי דְּרוֹב עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ וְכוּלֵי יְעוּיַּן מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי בָּזֶה לַהֲלָכָה בְּחִדּוּשַׁי].

And see Shabbat 23a that we recite the blessing "Who has sanctified us with His commandments" even over matters of doubt, with the exception of demai (doubtfully tithed produce) because the majority of common folk do tithe see my halakhic novellae on this.
דּוּגְמַת מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בִּתְשׁוּבַת הָרַ"ן הוּבָא בְּבֵית יוֹסֵף יוֹרֶה דֵעָה סִימָן רכ"ח, דְּכֵיוָן שֶׁמִּסָּפֵק צָרִיךְ חָשׁוּב כְּוַדַּאי יְעוּיַּן מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי בָּזֶה בְּחִדּוּשַׁי].
This parallels the responsum of the Ran cited in Beit Yosef (Yoreh De'ah 228), that whatever is obligatory out of doubt is legally treated as a certainty see my novellae on this.

וְכֵן מַשְׁמָע לְשׁוֹן הַגְּמָרָא בְּרָכוֹת ב' עַמּוּד ב': "מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁקִּידֵּשׁ הַיּוֹם בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת", עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּרַשִּׁ"י דְּהַיְינוּ בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת וְקָרוּי קִידֵּשׁ הַיּוֹם בִּקְדוּשַׁת שַׁבָּת.

And this is implied by the Gemara in Berakhot 2b: "from the time the day becomes sanctified on the eve of Shabbat," where Rashi explains that this refers to twilight (bein hashemashot), which is already titled "the day has become sanctified" through the sanctity of Shabbat.
[וְעַל שְׁעַת בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת יֵשׁ לוֹמַר גַּם אַשַּׁבָּת "יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּקַדְּשִׁינְהוּ לְשַׁבָּת", אַף דִּקְבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא, חוּמְרָא דְּסָפֵק הוּא מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל],

And regarding twilight, one could say even concerning Shabbat that "Israel sanctifies the Sabbath," for although Shabbat is inherently fixed and immutable, the stringency regarding twilight stems from Israel,
דְּכָל שֶׁבְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מַחֲמִירִים עַל עַצְמָם לַעֲשׂוֹתוֹ מִצְוָה – נַעֲשָׂה מִצְוָה וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה:
for whenever the children of Israel adopt a stringency to fulfill something as a mitzvah, it genuinely becomes a mitzvah and is imbued with holiness.

sections.en: The Working Hours of a Laborer Are Exclusively by Day

p: יז] זְמַן עֲבוֹדַת הַפּוֹעֵל רַק בַּיּוֹם כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "יֵצֵא אָדָם לְפָעֳלוֹ וְלַעֲבֹדָתוֹ] עֲדֵי עָרֶב",
The working hours of a laborer are exclusively by day, as written: "Man goes forth unto his work and to his labor until evening" (Psalms 104:23);
וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ בְּעֵירוּבִין (סה.): "אֲנַן פּוֹעֲלֵי דִימָמָא", אֲבָל לֵילְיָא לְשֵׁינְתָא,
and therefore they stated in Eruvin (65a): "We are day-laborers," whereas the night is allotted for sleep,
רַק כִּי יָזֵיף בִּימָמָא פָּרַע בְּלֵילְיָא וְעַיֵּין בְּתַלְמִידֵי רַבֵּנוּ יוֹנָה בְּרָכוֹת ח' עַמּוּד א' מַשְׁמָע דְּכֵן הֲלָכָה].
except that if one borrows from his daytime obligations, he repays at night and see Talmidei Rabbeinu Yonah on Berakhot 8a, implying that this is the halakhah.
רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם מָצָאנוּ גַּבֵּי מְלֶאכֶת בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ (בְּרָכוֹת ב' עַמּוּד ב') סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ דְּמַקְדְּמֵי וּמַחְשְׁכֵי גַּם בַּלַּיְלָה,
Nonetheless, regarding the work of the Temple (Berakhot 2b), the Gemara initially thought workers might arise early and work into the night;
וּלְמַסְקָנָא נַמֵּי רַק מִשּׁוּם דְּהוּצְרְכוּ הַלַּיְלָה לְמִשְׁמָר.
and its conclusion establishes that the night was required specifically for guard duty.
וְעַיֵּין שַׁבָּת פ"ט עַמּוּד ב' אָמְרִינַן: "דַּל פַּלְגָא דְּלֵילוֹתָא".
And see Shabbat 89b, where we subtract half of a person's lifetime on account of the nights spent asleep.
וְנִרְאֶה דְּגַם בְּכָל עֲבוֹדַת ה' הַלַּיְלָה רַק לְמִשְׁמָר,
It appears that in all divine service the night is designated primarily for guarding against harm,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, כז עַמּוּד א): "לְשָׁמְרָהּ" – זוֹ מִצְוַת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה,
as written in Zohar I:27a: "to guard it" refers to negative prohibitions;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֵירוּבִין צו.): דְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "הִשָּׁמֶר" וְכוּלֵי הוּא לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה,
and as taught in Eruvin (96a): wherever Scripture states "take heed / guard yourself," it denotes a negative prohibition,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲשֶׂה עֲבֵירוֹת,
meaning vigilance against sin,
וּלְכָךְ בְּשֵׁינָה דַּי, עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (יט:): "יָכוֹל יְגָרֶה עַצְמוֹ בְּשֵׁינָה וְכוּלֵי", עַיֵּין שָׁם:
and for this protective function sleep suffices, in line with Avodah Zarah (19b): "one might think a person should induce sleep to avoid sin, etc.," see there.

sections.en: The Evening Acceptance of Heaven's Yoke

p: יח] קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם דְּעַרְבִית, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה תְּלָאַתּוּ בִּשְׁכִיבָה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם עִיקָּרוֹ תָּלוּי בַּלַּיְלָה גַּם כֵּן,
The evening acceptance of Heaven's yoke, though framed scripturally around lying down, fundamentally depends on nighttime as well;
רַק שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ שְׁכִיבָה בַּלַּיְלָה נָקַט כֵּן קְרָא.
for Scripture utilized this term because reclining is the characteristic posture of night.
כִּי הַשְּׁכִיבָה מְיוּחֶדֶת לַלַּיְלָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ זְמַן פְּעוּלָה, אֲפִילּוּ אִי אִיכָּא אֱינָשֵׁי דִּבְזֶה סַגִּי, עַיֵּין ט' רֵישׁ עַמּוּד א' דְּגָנוּ בַּיּוֹם אֵינוֹ קָרוּי שְׁכִיבָה,
Reclining belongs uniquely to the night, an interval devoid of active labor; and even if some individuals sleep during the day, that daytime sleep is not biblically termed "lying down,"
לְפִי שֶׁהַיּוֹם מְיוּחָד לְקִימָה דְּהַיְינוּ עֲבוֹדָה.
because day is designated for rising—meaning active divine service.
כֵּן מַשְׁמָע דְּהָעִיקָּר בַּלַּיְלָה מִלְּשׁוֹן "מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁקִּידֵּשׁ וְכוּלֵי" בִּבְרָכוֹת ב' עַמּוּד ב',
That night is primary is evident from the Talmudic phrase "from the time the day is sanctified" (Berakhot 2b);
דְּקָשֶׁה עַל זֶה קוּשְׁיַת הַגְּמָרָא שָׁם: מִכְּדִי וְכוּלֵי לֵימָא מִשְּׁעַת בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת לְפִי פֵּירוּשׁ רַשִּׁ"י שָׁם,
for this answers the Gemara's query: let it plainly specify "from the time of twilight" according to Rashi's interpretation

[וְלוּלֵי פֵּירוּשׁ רַשִּׁ"י אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר דְּ"מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁקִּידֵּשׁ" הַיְינוּ תּוֹסֶפֶת שַׁבָּת, וְאִם כֵּן לָא קַשְׁיָא מִידֵי דְּיֵשׁ לוֹמַר דְּנָפְקָא מִינַּהּ אַבֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי עַיֵּין שָׁם בַּגְּמָרָא. וּלְפֵירוּשׁ רַשִּׁ"י צָרִיךְ לִדְחוֹק דְּתוֹסֶפֶת שַׁבָּת דְּרַבָּנָן וְהָכָא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא קָאָמַר, וְצָרִיךְ עִיּוּן],

and without Rashi's explanation one could suggest that "the day is sanctified" refers to the added margin of Shabbat (tosefet Shabbat), avoiding the difficulty, though according to Rashi one must answer that adding to Shabbat is rabbinic whereas our discussion concerns biblical law, which requires study,
דְּעַל זֶה לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ דְּקָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דִּקְדוּשַׁת הַיּוֹם מִבֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת, דְּזֶה עֲדַיִן לֹא נִשְׁמַע מִדְּבָרָיו אִם הָיָה מָקוֹם לְהִסְתַּפֵּק בָּזֶה,
since one cannot argue that it merely teaches that sanctity begins at twilight, as that inference would remain ambiguous had there been room for doubt;
אֶלָּא וַדַּאי דְּעִיקַּר קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע בַּלַּיְלָה,
rather, Shema fundamentally belongs to the night,
וּלְכָךְ מְצַיֵּין "מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁקִּידֵּשׁ הַיּוֹם" דִּלְעִנְיַן שַׁבָּת קָרוּי לַיְלָה,
and therefore the Gemara marks it by "the day is sanctified," since regarding Shabbat twilight is already legally deemed night;
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁכְּבָר מָצָאנוּ פַּעַם אַחַת דְּנִקְרָא לַיְלָה שַׁפִּיר יֵשׁ לוֹמַר גַּם זְמַן קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע אָז כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא דְּגָנוּ.
and since it is classified as night in one context, it serves as the time for Shema as well, as some people retire then.
כִּי עִיקַּר הַשְּׁכִיבָה מְיוּחָד לְעֵת הַחֹשֶׁךְ וְהֶעְדֵּר הָאוֹר וְהַבְּהִירוּת, אָז הוּא עֵת שְׁכִיבָה מֵעֲבוֹדָה
For reclining corresponds intrinsically to darkness and the absence of radiant clarity, being the time of withdrawal from work
וְרַק לְמִשְׁמָר מִמַּזִּיקִין שֶׁלֹּא לַעֲבוֹר עַל כָּל פָּנִים עֲבֵירוֹת אוֹ מִצְווֹת קְבוּעוֹת, עַיֵּין לְעֵיל אוֹת ט'.
serving only as protection from harmful forces to prevent sin, see Section 9.
וְכֵן מַשְׁמָע עוֹד שָׁם בַּגְּמָרָא: "וַהֲלֹא כֹּהֲנִים מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם הֵם טוֹבְלִים", מַשְׁמָע דְּאֵין סְבָרָא דְּיִהְיֶה זְמַן קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע דִּשְׁכִיבָה אָז מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם
This is further supported by the Gemara's query: "Do not priests immerse while it is yet day?"—implying it is illogical for the evening Shema of reclining to occur before nightfall
מִיהוּ זֶה יֵשׁ לוֹמַר פָּשׁוּט, דְּסָבַר הָא וַדַּאי אֵין דֶּרֶךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם שׁוֹכְבִים כָּל כָּךְ מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם],
though one could explain simply that people do not typically recline while it is still broad daylight,
כִּי הַיּוֹם לִמְלָאכָה, בְּעֵת הָאוֹר לֹא יֵשֵׁב בָּטֵל כְּיָשֵׁן:
for daytime is intended for labor, and amidst light a person should not sit idle like one asleep.

sections.en: In All Matters and in the Division of Times Embedded within the Fabric Of…

p: יט] בְּכָל הָעִנְיָנִים וּמַעֲשֵׂה חֲלוּקַּת הַזְּמַנִּים שֶׁמּוּטְבָּעִים בָּעוֹלָם וְהַנְהָגָתוֹ הֵם גַּם כֵּן כֵּן אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
In all matters and in the division of times embedded within the fabric of creation and its governance, the same dynamic exists with the Blessed Name,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק הָרוֹאֶה (בְּרָכוֹת נח.): "מַלְכוּתָא דִרְקִיעָא כְּמַלְכוּתָא דְאַרְעָא",
as taught in Berakhot 58a: "The kingdom of Heaven corresponds to the kingdom of earth,"
וְכֵן אִיתָא בִּבְרָכוֹת ג' עַמּוּד א': "אִיכָּא מִשְׁמוֹרוֹת בָּרָקִיעַ כִּי הֵיכִי דְּאִיכָּא (כֵּן הוּא גִּרְסַת הָרֹא"שׁ) בְּאַרְעָא",
and as stated in Berakhot 3a: "There are watches in the heavens just as there are on earth" (the reading of the Rosh),
וְהוּא לְגַבֵּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּדְמַסַּיֵּים "וְעַל כָּל מִשְׁמָר וְכוּלֵי"
and this applies directly in relation to the Blessed Name, as the passage concludes: "and over every watch the Holy One roars..."
וְרַשִּׁ"י שֶׁפֵּירֵשׁ אַמַּלְאָכִים – לֹא יָדַעְתִּי לָמָּה לֵיהּ;
and why Rashi interpreted this as referring to angels, I do not know;

אֲבָל קוּשְׁטָא כֵּן, דִּלְשׁוֹן 'מִשְׁמוֹרוֹת' כְּמוֹ מִשְׁמְרוֹת כְּהֻנָּה שׁוֹמְרֵי בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, וְכֵן לִמְלָכִים שׁוֹמְרִים בַּלֵּילוֹת וּמִתְחַלְּפִים בְּכָל מִשְׁמָר, וְזֶהוּ ג' מִשְׁמוֹרוֹת, וְכֵן בְּמַלְכוּתָא דִרְקִיעָא.
for the truth is that 'watches' resembles the priestly watches guarding the Temple, or royal night sentries rotating every watch—hence three watches, mirrored identically in the Heavenly kingdom.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּאַרְעָא נִיכָּר חֲלוּקַּת הַזְּמַן לְכָל אָדָם כִּדְמַסַּיֵּים "חֲמוֹר וְכוּלֵי", כֵּן בָּרָקִיעַ נִיכָּר גַּם לְגַבֵּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נֶגֶד לְמַטָּה.

And just as on earth the temporal division is evident to all people through earthly signs—donkey braying, etc.—so too in the heavens is it reflected before the Blessed Name facing the terrestrial realm below.
וְרָאוּי לְדָבְקָה בּוֹ וּלְהִתְבּוֹנֵן בְּמַעֲשֵׂה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת גַּם כֵּן כֵּן,
It is fitting to cleave unto Him and contemplate the workings of the Blessed Name in order to emulate them,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרֹא"שׁ שָׁם אַהָא דִּ"וְעַל כָּל מִשְׁמָר", לָכֵן רָאוּי לְכָל יְרֵא שָׁמַיִם וְכוּלֵי.
as the Rosh wrote concerning Hashem roaring at each watch, that every God-fearing person should awaken and lament at those moments.
וְהַהִתְבּוֹנְנוּת הוּא כְּפִי עִנְיַן הַזְּמַן, וּבַלַּיְלָה שֶׁהוּא רוֹמֵז זְמַן הַגָּלוּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "שֹׁמֵר מַה מִּלַּיְלָה", הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יוֹשֵׁב וְשׁוֹאֵג וְכוּלֵי:

This contemplation corresponds to the character of the specific hour: at night, which alludes to exile—as written, "Watchman, what of the night?" (Isaiah 21:11)—the Holy One sits and roars over the destruction and dispersal of His children.

sections.en: There Are Watches in the Heavens"—referring to Celestial Spiritual Matters

p: כ] אִיכָּא מִשְׁמוֹרוֹת בָּרָקִיעַ – לְדִבְרֵי רְקִיעִיִּים, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר לַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
"There are watches in the heavens"—referring to celestial spiritual matters, meaning the service of the Blessed Name,
כִּי הֵיכִי דְּאִיכָּא בְּאַרְעָא – בָּעִנְיָנִים הַפְּחוּתִים וַעֲבוֹדַת הָאֲדָמָה.
"just as there are on earth"—in mundane agricultural labors and terrestrial occupations.
כֵּן מַמָּשׁ דּוּגְמָתוֹ, וּמִמֶּנּוּ נִקַּח לַעֲבוֹד ה' בְּאוֹתוֹ עֵת] בְּעִנְיָן זֶה.
They run precisely parallel, and from the earthly signs we derive our model for serving Hashem at that time.
סִימָן לַדָּבָר: מִשְׁמָר א' – חֲמוֹר נוֹעֵר:
A sign for this: during the first watch, the donkey brays.
הַחֹמֶר דּוּגְמַת חֲמוֹר, עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ "עַם הַדּוֹמֶה לַחֲמוֹר" גַּם הוּא נוֹעֵר כַּחֲמוֹר לְמַשׂוֹי הַמִּצְווֹת בִּכְלֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה.
The material body (chomer, playing on chamor / donkey, as in "a people resembling a donkey") likewise brays under the heavy burden of mitzvot through the physical instruments of action.
ב' – כְּלָבִים צוֹעֲקִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר: צָוְוחִין כְּכַלְבָּא, בִּתְפִלָּה
Second watch: dogs bark; as the Zohar states, they cry out like dogs in urgent prayer
וְהַכְּלָבִים עַזֵּי פָנִים, וְכֵן חוּצְפָּה בִּתְפִלָּה כְּלַפֵּי שְׁמַיָּא מַהֲנְיָא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּתַעֲנִית ח' עַמּוּד א'.
and dogs are brazen, just as spiritual brazenness in prayer directed toward Heaven is effective (Ta'anit 8a).
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת קנה:): "לֵית דְּעַנְיָא מִכַּלְבָּא" – עָנִי בְּדַעַת, וְאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא תְּפִלָּה,
As they taught in Shabbat 155b: "none is poorer than a dog"—signifying one impoverished in understanding, possessing nothing other than desperate prayer,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה לח): אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין אָנוּ יוֹדְעִין וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
as described in Shemot Rabbah 38: "they said to Him: we know nothing, we have only our prayers," see there.
ג' – תִּינוֹק יוֹנֵק, הַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה,
Third watch: an infant suckles—which represents Torah study,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק עַרְבֵי פְסָחִים (פְּסָחִים קיב.): "מִמַּה שֶּׁהָעֵגֶל רוֹצֶה לִינַק", שֶׁתּוֹרָה נִמְשְׁלָה לְחָלָב.
as taught in Pesachim 112a: "more than the calf wishes to suckle the cow wishes to nurse," for Torah is likened to milk.
וְאִשָּׁה וְכוּלֵי הַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּיבָמוֹת ס"ג עַמּוּד ב'.
And "a woman conversing with her husband" (Berakhot 3a) likewise represents Torah, as expounded in Yevamot 63b.
רַק הָאִשָּׁה הִיא הַמֵּינֶקֶת וְהַיְינוּ גְּדוֹלֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְתִינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן מְקַבְּלִין מֵהֶם.
Only here the woman is the nursing mother representing the great leaders of Israel, while school children receive the flow of Torah from them.
וְהֵם תּוֹרָה וַעֲבוֹדָה וּגְמִילוּת חֲסָדִים
And these three watches represent Torah, prayerful divine service, and acts of kindness
וְכֵן תּוֹרָה וּתְפִלָּה וְקָרְבָּנוֹת (הַיְינוּ מַעֲשֶׂה) בִּשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה שָׁם],
and likewise Torah, prayer, and sacrifices (action) in Shemot Rabbah there,
שֶׁהֵם נֶגֶד מַחֲשָׁבָה, דִּבּוּר וּמַעֲשֶׂה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר.
which correspond to thought, speech, and action, as I explained elsewhere.
רַק שֶׁבַּלַּיְלָה בְּעֵת הַחֹשֶׁךְ הֵם הֲפוּכִים, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר:

Except that at night during darkness their developmental sequence is inverted: starting with physical action (the donkey), progressing through speech and prayer (the dogs), and culminating in pure thought and Torah (the nursing child), as I have elucidated elsewhere.

sections.en: An Awakening from Below in the Service of Hashem Arouses a Corresponding Movement Above

p: כא] אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא בַּעֲבוֹדַת ה' מְעוֹרֵר לְמַעְלָה דּוּגְמָתוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים.
An awakening from below in the service of Hashem arouses a corresponding movement Above, as written in the Zohar multiple times.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (חֲגִיגָה טו:): אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר שִׁילָא לְאֵלִיָּהוּ וְכוּלֵי, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עַכְשָׁו אָמַר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
And as they said (Chagigah 15b): Rabbah bar Shila found Elijah, etc., and Elijah told him: "Right now the Holy One is reciting a teaching in the name of Rabbi Meir"
וּכְעֵין זֶה בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּגִטִּין (ו':) בְּרַבִּי אֶבְיָתָר].
and similarly in the first chapter of Gittin (6b) regarding Rabbi Evyatar.
וְזֶהוּ "אִיכָּא מִשְׁמוֹרוֹת בָּרָקִיעַ כִּי הֵיכִי דְּאִיכָּא בְּאַרְעָא"
And this is the meaning of "there are watches in the heavens just as there are on earth"—
שֶׁמִּתְעוֹרְרִים בְּאַרְעָא כְּפִי הַסִּימָן דִּיְהֵיב:
that souls are aroused on earth in accordance with the specific terrestrial signs provided in the Talmud.

sections.en: The Night Comprises Three Distinct Watches and Divisions of Time

p: כב] ג' מִשְׁמוֹרוֹת וּזְמַנִּים חֲלוּקִים הָוֵי הַלַּיְלָה
The night comprises three distinct watches and divisions of time
וְעַיֵּין שָׁם עַמּוּד ב' דִּלְחַד מַאן דְּאָמַר ד'.
and see there (Berakhot 3b) that according to one opinion there are four.
וְאוֹתָם הַיּוֹדְעֵי בִינָה לַעִתִּים יֵשׁ לָהֶם גַּם כֵּן לְחַלֵּק הַלַּיְלָה לְג' מִשְׁמוֹרוֹת וּזְמַנִּים, כָּל מִשְׁמָר הוּא זְמַן בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ,
And those who possess discernment of the times must likewise divide the spiritual night into three distinct watches and phases, each watch constituting a specific spiritual epoch in its own right;
וְכֵן חֶשְׁכַּת הָאוֹר וְכֵן הוּא זְמַן הַגָּלוּת חָלוּק לְג' עִתִּים אֵלּוּ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר:
and so too the obscurity of light, and so too the prolonged era of exile, is subdivided into these three developmental phases, as I explained elsewhere.

sections.en: In Every Divine Act of the Blessed Name There Is an Identifiable Sign Reflected…

p: כג] בְּכָל מַעֲשֵׂה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יֵשׁ סִימָן נִיכָּר לְמַטָּה,
In every divine act of the Blessed Name there is an identifiable sign reflected below,

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר לִקּוּטֵי אֲמָרִים מֵהָרַב הַמַּגִּיד מִמֶּזְרִיטְשׁ זְצוֹקַ"ל, כִּי חִסָּרוֹן שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לַצַּדִּיק הוּא לְסִימָן לוֹ שֶׁיֵּדַע שֶׁאוֹתוֹ הַחִסָּרוֹן בַּשְּׁכִינָה כִּבְיָכוֹל, עַיֵּין שָׁם בְּבֵיאוּרוֹ.

and as written in Sefer Likkutei Amarim by the Maggid of Mezritch, that any personal lack befalling a righteous person serves as a sign to inform him that this very deficiency exists, as it were, within the Shechinah, see there in his explanation.
וְזֶהוּ "עַל כָּל מִשְׁמָר שׁוֹאֵג וְכוּלֵי וְסִימָן לַדָּבָר" – רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁיֵּשׁ סִימָן נִיכָּר לְמַטָּה.
And this is the meaning of "over each watch He roars, etc., and a sign for the matter is..."—meaning that there is a discernible corresponding sign manifest down below on earth.
וּשְׁאָגָה א', שֶׁהוּא בְּמִשְׁמָר א' דְּגָלוּת, כָּל כָּךְ בְּתוֹקֶף עַד שֶׁנִּיכָּר גַּם בַּחֲמוֹר שֶׁהוּא בְּרִיָּה פְּחוּתָה בְּיוֹתֵר,
The first roar, which corresponds to the first watch of exile, is of such overpowering intensity that it reverberates even within the donkey, the lowliest of beasts,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב "עַם הַדּוֹמֶה לַחֲמוֹר", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּבָבָא קַמָּא (צב:): "קַרְיָיךְ חַמְרָא וְכוּלֵי".
as Scripture alludes to "a people resembling a donkey," and as the Sages noted in Bava Kamma (92b): "If someone calls you a donkey, etc."
וּבַשְּׁנִיָּה רַק בִּכְלָבִים שֶׁאֵין פְּחוּתִים כָּל כָּךְ, שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ צַד אֶחָד דִּקְדוּשָׁה,
In the second watch, the reaction is felt only in dogs, which are not quite as base, possessing an aspect of sanctity,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בָּבָא קַמָּא ס:): כְּלָבִים מְשַׂחֲקִים וְכוּלֵי כְּלָבִים בּוֹכִים וְכוּלֵי,
as written in Bava Kamma (60b): "When dogs frolic, Elijah has arrived; when dogs howl, the Angel of Death is in town,"
דְּכֶלֶב בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא אֵלִיָּהוּ
for kelev (dog,
shares the numerical value of Eliyahu
(א-ל-י-ה-ו = 52) (עַיֵּין פֵּירוּשׁ פֶּרֶק שִׁירָה בְּסִדּוּר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב עֶמְדִּין).
(see the commentary to Perek Shirah in the prayer book of the Yaavetz).
כִּי יֵשׁ עַזּוּת דִּקְדוּשָׁה: "עַז כַּנָּמֵר"
For there exists holy brazenness, as in "be bold as a leopard"
זֶהוּ דּוּגְמַת קִנְאַת פִּינְחָס, זֶה אֵלִיָּהוּ].
which is exemplified by the holy zeal of Phinehas, who is Elijah.
וּלְלִישָׁנָא דְּאֶמְצָעִית דְּאֶמְצָעִיתָא, הַיְינוּ חֲצוֹת, עֵת רָצוֹן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב יְבָמוֹת ע"ב עַמּוּד א',
And according to the formulation locating this watch at the deep midpoint of the night, namely midnight, it is a period of supreme divine favor (et ratzon) as noted in Yevamot 72a;
לְכָךְ הַסִּימָן "כְּלָבִים צוֹעֲקִים", וְהַיְינוּ הֲרָמַת קוֹל שִׂמְחָה: אֵלִיָּהוּ בָּא לָעִיר, שֶׁהוּא סִימַן עֵת רָצוֹן,
therefore the sign is "dogs crying out," which signifies raising a voice of joy because Elijah has entered the city, marking an acceptable time of favor,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "הִנְנִי שֹׁלֵחַ לָכֶם אֵת אֵלִיָּה הַנָּבִיא לִפְנֵי בּוֹא יוֹם ה' וְגוֹמֵר".
as written: "Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and awesome day of the Lord" (Malachi 3:23).
כִּי מֵחֲצוֹת וְאֵילָךְ מַתְחִיל הַרְגָּשַׁת הַיּוֹם, עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "מִשְׁמוּרָה וּפַלְגָא נַמֵּי הָוֵי מִשְׁמוֹרוֹת".
For from midnight onward the illumination of the daytime begins to be perceived, in line with the Talmudic principle that "a watch and a half is also classified as a watch."
וּבַשְּׁלִישִׁית הַהַרְגָּשָׁה רַק לִבְנֵי אָדָם שְׁלֵמִים,
In the third watch, spiritual awareness is felt exclusively by fully developed human beings;
וּלְפִי שֶׁקָּרוֹב לְאוֹר הַיּוֹם הֵם מִתְעוֹרְרִים עַל יְדֵי הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּשְׁאָגָה דִּלְעֵילָא, שֶׁהוּא מִתּוֹךְ הַרְגָּשַׁת הָאוֹר.
and because the light of day draws near, they are awakened through the supernal roar Above, which emerges directly out of sensing the approaching light.
וְכֵן הֵם מִתְעוֹרְרִים בְּסִיפּוּר דְּחִיבָּה: אִשָּׁה לְבַעְלָהּ
And so they awaken in an intimate discourse of love: a woman with her husband
כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים],
the Congregation of Israel and the Blessed Name, as portrayed in the Song of Songs,
וְתִינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן יוֹנְקִים מִשְּׁדֵי כְּלַל הַכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יְדֵי שֶׁמִּתְעוֹרְרִים לִינַק,
and school children suckling from the nurturing breasts of the collective assembly of Israel as they awaken to nurse.
וְכַהַרְגָּשָׁה לְמַטָּה בִּפְשִׁיטוּת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה, אֲבָל רַק בְּמִין הָאָדָם.
And this matches the literal physical perception below, yet occurring strictly within the human species.
וּבָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת אֵין בְּנֵי אָדָם מִתְעוֹרְרִים, שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ תּוֹקֶף הַחֹשֶׁךְ אִי אֶפְשָׁר לַהַרְגָּשָׁה לִהְיוֹת מִכֹּחַ הָאָדָם שֶׁבָּאִישׁ, רַק מִכֹּחַ הַחֹמֶר:

In the earlier watches human beings do not awaken, for amid the crushing darkness of the initial hours it is impossible for sensitivity to emerge from the human, transcendent faculty within man, but only from the brute material nature.

sections.en: During the First Watch of the Night the Donkey Brays

p: כד] מִשְׁמוֹר א' בַּלַּיְלָה: חֲמוֹר נוֹעֵר, שֶׁנֵּיעוֹר עֲדַיִן לְפִי שֶׁהוּא זְמַן שֶׁהוֹלְכִין לִשְׁכַּב רוֹב בְּנֵי אָדָם
During the first watch of the night the donkey brays, being still awake because that is the timeframe in which the majority of people retire to sleep

[דְּלָא תֵימָא דְּמַה דְּאִיכָּא דְּהוֹלְכִים לִשְׁכַּב יוֹעִיל כִּדְלָדִידַן אִיכָּא דְּגָנוּ, דְּאִם כֵּן כָּל הַלַּיְלָה נַמֵּי, עַיֵּין בְּרַשִׁ"י וְתוֹסָפוֹת ט' עַמּוּד א' דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "וּבִלְבַד", דְּיֵשׁ שֶׁהוֹלְכִים אָז תְּחִלַּת שְׁכִיבָה],

lest you suggest that merely because some people are retiring to bed it suffices just as we find 'some people are sleeping,' for were that so, the whole night would qualify as well; see Rashi and Tosafot on 9a, s.v. u'vilvad, that some begin sleeping then,
עַיֵּין בְּתַלְמִידֵי רַבֵּנוּ יוֹנָה בַּמִּשְׁנָה דְּרֵישׁ בְּרָכוֹת
see Talmidei Rabbeinu Yonah on the opening Mishna of Berakhot
אֱלִיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וְהוּא הַדִּין לְדִידַן.
according to Rabbi Eliezer, and the same principle applies to our own practice.
וּלְכָךְ נֵיעוֹר עִם בְּעָלָיו עֲדַיִן בְּסוֹף מִשְׁמָר א', אֲבָל לְהַלָּאָה קָשׁוּר עַל אֲבוּסוֹ.
And therefore the donkey remains awake with its owner until the end of the first watch, but afterward it is tied fast to its feeding trough.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן כֶּלֶב, אֵין בְּעָלָיו קוֹשְׁרוֹ בַּאֲבוּס
By contrast, as for a dog, its owner does not tether it to a trough
רֶמֶז "אֲנִי יְשֵׁנָה וְלִבִּי עֵר", צְעָקָה בִּתְפִלָּה עֲבוֹדָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב],
an allusion to "I sleep, but my heart is awake" (Song of Songs 5:2), representing the outcry of prayer, the service of the heart,
וּבִתְחִלַּת (לְלִישָׁנָא קַמָּא) מִשְׁמָר ג' שׁוּב נֵיעוֹרִים, אִם כֵּן אֵין זְמַן שֵׁינָה רַק מִשְׁמָר אֶחָד, הַיְינוּ ד' שָׁעוֹת;
and at the start (according to the first Talmudic phrasing) of the third watch people awaken again, which means the duration of genuine sleep is only one single watch, namely four hours;
וּלְלִישָׁנָא ב' דִּבְסוֹף מִשְׁמָר ג' נֵיעוֹרִים, זְמַן שֵׁינָה ח' שָׁעוֹת,
whereas according to the second phrasing where people awaken at the end of the third watch, the duration of sleep spans eight hours;
וְזֶהוּ כְּדִבְרֵי הָרַמְבַּ"ם בְּהִלְכוֹת דֵּעוֹת דְּפָסַק כְּלִישָׁנָא בַּתְרָא כְּדַרְכּוֹ.
and this agrees with Maimonides in Hilkhot De'ot (4:4), who codified following the latter formulation, according to his usual method.
וְעַיֵּין בְּתוֹסָפוֹת עֵירוּבִין ס"ה עַמּוּד א' דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "אֶלָּא", יֵשׁ לוֹמַר לֵילֵי תְּקוּפַת תַּמּוּז הֵם ח' שָׁעוֹת בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
And see Tosafot in Eruvin 65a (s.v. ela), where one may explain that the nights of the Tammuz solstice span eight hours in the Land of Israel.
וְעַיֵּין שִׁילְהֵי תַּעֲנִית ל"א עַמּוּד א' דְּמִטַּ"וּ בְּאָב צָרִיךְ לְהוֹסִיף, וְהַיְינוּ מֵחֲצִי תְּקוּפַת תַּמּוּז, דְּמֵחֲצִי וּלְמַעְלָה מַתְחִיל לְהִתְגַּדֵּל הַלַּיְלָה.

And see the end of Ta'anit (31a) that from the fifteenth of Av one must add time to Torah study, which corresponds to the midpoint of the Tammuz solstice, since from the midpoint onward the night begins to lengthen.
וְגַם לְפִי שֶׁהַחֲצִי לְעוֹלָם כְּסִיּוּם וְעַד הַחֲצִי כְּהַתְחָלָה, לְפִי שֶׁרוּבּוֹ כְּכֻלּוֹ בְּכָל מָקוֹם,
Furthermore, the midpoint consistently functions like a conclusion, and up to the midpoint functions as a beginning, because 'the majority is like the whole' across all halakhic matters;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר טַעַם תְּפִלַּת הַשַּׁחַר עַד חֲצוֹת מִשּׁוּם דְּמִשְׁמוּרָה וּפַלְגָא וְכוּלֵי.
as I explained elsewhere regarding the reason morning prayer extends until midday, because 'a watch and a half' shares that dynamic.
וְעַיֵּין סֻכָּה כ"ו עַמּוּד ב'.
And see Sukkah 26b.
וְהָאֲרִ"י זַ"ל כָּתַב דְּשִׁיתִּין נִשְׁמֵי – ו' שָׁעוֹת, עַיֵּין בְּמִקְדַּשׁ מֶלֶךְ וַיִּגַּשׁ ר"ז עַמּוּד א', וְיְעוּיַּן מַה שֶּׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּחִדּוּשַׁי:
And the holy Ari of blessed memory wrote that sixty breaths of sleep equal six hours, see Mikdash Melekh on Vayigash 207a, and see what I elaborated in my novellae.

sections.en: During the Second Watch Dogs Cry Out

p: כה] מִשְׁמוֹר ב': כְּלָבִים צוֹעֲקִים, כְּשֶׁהַכֹּל יְשֵׁנִים,
During the second watch dogs cry out, when everyone is deeply asleep,
דִּבְמִשְׁמוֹר א' יֵשׁ בְּנֵי אָדָם נֵיעוֹרִים וְאֵין מַנִּיחִים אוֹתוֹ.
for during the first watch there are people still awake who would disturb him.
וְכֵן תְּפִלָּה טוֹב בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁאֵין בְּנֵי אָדָם, כִּי הֵם מְבַלְבְּלִים אוֹתוֹ בִּפְנִיּוֹת וּמַחֲשֶׁבֶת חוּץ, וּשְׁאָר מַחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת בָּא עַל יְדֵי כֵּן,

And similarly, prayer is best in a secluded place where people are absent, because other people distract a person with self-conscious motives and external thoughts, through which extraneous distractions penetrate,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּדֶגֶל מַחֲנֵה אֶפְרַיִם כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים עַל פָּסוּק "וְכָל אָדָם לֹא יִהְיֶה בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד בְּבֹאוֹ לְכַפֵּר בַּקֹּדֶשׁ".
as written in Degel Machaneh Ephraim numerous times on the verse: "And no man shall be in the Tent of Meeting when he goes in to make atonement in the holy place" (Leviticus 16:17).
וּתְפִלָּה בְּצִיבּוּר – כְּשֶׁגַּם הַצִּיבּוּר מִתְפַּלְּלִין אֵין דַּעְתָּן עָלָיו וְכֵן הוּא עֲלֵיהֶם.
And regarding communal prayer: when the entire congregation is actively praying, their attention is not focused on him, nor is his attention on them.
וְגַם בַּתּוֹרָה אָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים קיב.): "לֹא תִשְׁנֶה בְּגוֹבְהָהּ שֶׁל עִיר",
And regarding Torah study as well they said (Pesachim 112a): "Do not study at the highest thoroughfare of the city,"
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ (נְדָרִים פא.): "הִזָּהֲרוּ בַּחֲבוּרָה" וְכֵן בְּכָל מָקוֹם
even though they stated (Nedarim 81a): "Be heedful of studying in a group," and in multiple sources—
הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁלּוֹמֵד עִמָּהֶם, אֲבָל לֹא בִּמְקוֹם בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁאֵין לוֹמְדִין עִמּוֹ.
meaning specifically when one studies alongside them, but not in a place populated by people who are not studying with him.
וַאֲפִילּוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּנֵי אָדָם צָרִיךְ לְצַיֵּיר בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ כְּאִילּוּ אֵין אִישׁ בָּעוֹלָם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּדֶגֶל מַחֲנֵה אֶפְרַיִם שָׁם.
And even if people are present, one must picture in his mind as though no human being exists in the world, as written in Degel Machaneh Ephraim there.
וּלְלִישָׁנָא דְּאֶמְצָעִית דְּאֶמְצָעִיתָא, לְפִי שֶׁאָז תּוֹקֶף הַשֵּׁינָה, כִּי בְּסוֹף א' מַתְחִילִין וּבִתְחִלַּת ג' נֵיעוֹרִין,

And according to the formulation locating this watch at the very midpoint, it is because sleep is then at its deepest intensity, for people begin sleeping at the end of the first watch and awaken at the start of the third,
וַאֲפִילּוּ יִצְעֲקוּ לֹא יֵעוֹרוּ.
such that even if dogs cry out, people will not awaken.
וְכָךְ צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת הַשֵּׁינָה בְּלִבּוֹ מִכָּל עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
And such must be the complete slumber within a person's heart regarding all affairs of this mundane world,
שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ עַל יְדֵי הַצְּעָקָה בִּתְפִלָּה "בָּרֵךְ עָלֵינוּ אֶת הַשָּׁנָה" וְכַיּוֹצֵא לֹא יֵעוֹרוּ,
that even through the urgent petition of prayer—such as "Bless for us this year" and the like—the heart's worldly attachments should not awaken,
רַק יְכַוֵּין הַכֹּל צֹרֶךְ גָּבוֹהַּ כַּיָּדוּעַ,
rather he directs everything purely toward Supernal divine needs, as is known,
וְכָל עִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה יִהְיוּ בְּטֵלִים אֶצְלוֹ, דִּכְיָשֵׁן דָּמֵי:
and all worldly physical matters remain nullified before him, being comparable to one asleep.

sections.en: During the Third Watch an Infant Nurses and a Woman Converses with Her Husband.…

p: כו] מִשְׁמוֹר ג': תִּינוֹק יוֹנֵק וְאִשָּׁה מְסַפֶּרֶת. שְׁנֵיהֶם יַחַד זֶהוּ רַק בְּמִשְׁמָר ג' שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כֻּלָּם נֵיעוֹרִים בִּזְמַן אֶחָד.
During the third watch an infant nurses and a woman converses with her husband. Both occurring together happens only in the third watch, when everyone awakens at the same time.
וְכֵן בַּנִּמְשָׁל: יְנִיקַת תִּינוֹק מִשְּׁדֵי אִמּוֹ הַתּוֹרָה כַּאֲשֶׁר אִשָּׁה מְסַפֶּרֶת, וְיִהְיֶה גַּם הָאָב
And so too in the spiritual metaphor: the nursing of the child from the breasts of his mother, the Torah, takes place when the woman converses, so that the Father as well
הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק כָּל מָקוֹם]
the Holy One, blessed be He, as I wrote in my commentary on the chapter Kol Makom
מִשְׁתַּעֲשֵׁעַ בִּינִיקַת הַתִּינוֹק, זֶהוּ רַק בְּמִשְׁמוֹר ג' שֶׁכְּבָר שָׁלֵם בַּמַּעֲשִׂים וּבַעֲבוֹדָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב.
delights in the nursing of the child, which occurs solely in the third watch, when one has already reached perfection in physical deeds and in the interior service of the heart.
וְהִנֵּה בַּמַּעֲשֶׂה הִקְדִּים תִּינוֹק יוֹנֵק, שֶׁהוּא הַמְּעוֹרֵר קוֹדֶם לָאֵם, וְהִיא מְעוֹרֶרֶת לַבַּעַל.
Now in practical reality, the text placed the nursing infant first, for he awakens the mother first, and she in turn arouses the husband.

אֲבָל לְהַלָּן בִּשְׁמִיעָה לַאֲחֵרִים, לְמַאן דְּגָנֵי וְכוּלֵי, אָמַר לְהֵיפֶךְ: "אִשָּׁה מְסַפֶּרֶת", שֶׁקּוֹלָם נִשְׁמָע וְשׁוֹמֵעַ קוֹדֶם, וְאַחַר כָּךְ כְּשֶׁמַּטֶּה אָזְנוֹ שָׁמַע קוֹל תִּינוֹק יוֹנֵק.

But further on regarding hearing by outside observers—for one sleeping in a dark room—it stated the reverse: "a woman converses," because their spoken voice carries far and is heard first, and only afterward, when leaning his ear, does he detect the soft sound of the nursing infant.
וְהַנִּמְשָׁל: יְנִיקַת תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן מִשְּׁדֵי אִמָּם
And the spiritual parallel: the suckling of school children from the breasts of their mother
כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק כָּל מָקוֹם],
the Congregation of Israel, as I wrote at the beginning of the chapter Kol Makom,
רָאשֵׁי הַדּוֹר, וְהֵם אָז מְסַפְּרִים כְּבוֹד אֵל וּשְׁכִינָה מְדַבֶּרֶת מִתּוֹךְ גְּרוֹנָם
namely the leaders of the generation, who at that hour recount the glory of God while the Shechinah speaks through their throat
וְזֶהוּ בְּמִשְׁמוֹר ג' שֶׁל גָּלוּת הַדּוֹמֶה לְלַיְלָה].
and this corresponds to the third watch of the exile, which is likened to night.
בֶּאֱמֶת תִּינוֹק יוֹנֵק קוֹדֶם,
In essential reality, the infant suckling precedes;
רַק לְהַרְגָּשַׁת עֵין בְּנֵי אָדָם אִשָּׁה מְסַפֶּרֶת קוֹדֶם.
yet to the outward perception of human eyes, the woman conversing appears first.

וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר תּוֹלְדוֹת יַעֲקֹב יוֹסֵף עַל פָּסוּק "גָּמַר חָסִיד כִּי פַסּוּ אֱמוּנִים" בְּשֵׁם רַבִּי לֵיבּ פִּיסְטִינֶער, דְּהַאי קְרָא מֵרֵישֵׁיהּ לְסֵיפֵיהּ וּמִסֵּיפֵיהּ לְרֵישֵׁיהּ מִדְרַשׁ.

And as written in Sefer Toledot Yaakov Yosef on the verse "The pious man has ceased, for the faithful fail" (Psalms 12:2) in the name of Rabbi Leib Pistiner, that this verse may be expounded from its beginning to its end, and from its end to its beginning.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֲרָכִין יז.): פַּרְנָס לְפִי הַדּוֹר, דּוֹר לְפִי פַּרְנָס, וְהֵי קָדִים כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:
And as they said (Arachin 17a): "A leader is according to the generation, and a generation is according to its leader," and which one precedes depends on the perspective, as noted above.

sections.en: At the Beginning of the Day and Likewise at the Beginning of the Night

p: כז] צָרִיךְ בִּתְחִלַּת יוֹם וְכֵן בִּתְחִלַּת לַיְלָה לְהִתְפַּלֵּל עַל הַגָּלוּת
At the beginning of the day and likewise at the beginning of the night, one must pray over the exile
שִׁעְבּוּד וְכוּלֵי וּשְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה שְׁקוּלִים, וְהַכֹּל אֶחָד],
for physical subjugation and the inner leaven in the dough are equivalent, being all one,
וְעַיֵּין בְּמָגֵן אַבְרָהָם רֵישׁ סִימָן א' בְּשֵׁם שְׁלָ"ה.
and see Magen Avraham at the beginning of Siman 1 in the name of the Shelah.
לְפִי שֶׁאָז הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שׁוֹאֵג וְכוּלֵי
For at those transition points the Holy One, blessed be He, roars over the destruction
וּכְדִיָלֵיף בְּהָרֹא"שׁ עַל סוֹף כָּל מִשְׁמָר מִזֶּה],
as the Rosh derived concerning the end of each watch from this,
כִּדְמַשְׁמָע מִלְּשׁוֹן הַגְּמָרָא: סִימָנָא לְמַאי לִי? אוּרְתָּא סִימָנָא לְמַאי לִי? יְמָמָא הוּא!
as implied by the wording of the Gemara (Berakhot 3a): "Why do I need a sign? For the evening, why do I need a sign? It is daytime!"

דְּקָשֶׁה, הָא מָצִינוּ בְּיוֹמָא (כח.) שֶׁטָּעוּ בִּמְאוֹר הַלְּבָנָה שֶׁהוּא אוֹר הַיּוֹם, וְכֵן מָצִינוּ לְהַלָּן (כז עַמּוּד ב) בְּיוֹם הַמְּעוּנָּן הִתְפַּלְּלוּ שֶׁל שַׁבָּת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת, וְאִם כֵּן שַׁפִּיר צָרִיךְ סִימָנָא כְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ נִיכָּר.

for this poses a difficulty: do we not find in Yoma (28a) that they mistook the moonlight for the break of day, and do we not find below (27b) that on an overcast day they prayed the Shabbat prayer on Friday afternoon, showing that one indeed requires a sign when it is not obvious?
וְעַל כָּרְחֲךָ דְּהַךְ סִימָן פֵּירוּשׁ סִימָן עַל אֲמִירַת הַשְּׁאָגָה,
Therefore perforce this Talmudic sign refers to identifying the precise moment of the Supernal Roar;
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר דְּלַיְלָה וִימָמָא הוּא, וְאִם כֵּן אֵין צָרִיךְ סִימָן טְפֵי
and to this the Gemara responded that night and day are inherently distinct, so that one requires no additional sign
נִיכָּר לְמַטָּה כִּדְמִשְׁתָּעֵינָא לְעֵיל אוֹת כג],
discernible below, as explained above in Section 23,

כִּי וַדַּאי בְּהַתְחָלַת הַזְּמַן דְּלַיְלָה וּדְיוֹם, שֶׁהוּא חֲלִיפוֹת זְמַן דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, אָז שׁוֹאֵג עַל הַחוּרְבָּן, שֶׁכְּבָר מַתְחִיל עוֹד זְמַן בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ מִזְּמַנֵּי הָעוֹלָם וַעֲדַיִן בֶּן דָּוִד לֹא בָּא.

because certainly at the inception of night and at the inception of day—which represent the structural shifts of this physical world—He roars over the destruction, seeing that yet another independent epoch of world-time begins while the son of David has still not arrived.

וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר נַמֵּי לְהַלָּן: לְמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ? לִמְקְרֵי קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע, דְּקָשֶׁה, לְמַאי לִי "לְמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ וְכוּלֵי", וְכִי לְעֵיל קָאָמַר נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ? וַהֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵימַר רַק: סִימָנָא לְמַאן דְּגָנֵי בְּבַיִת אָפֵל.

And this explains what the Gemara states further: "What is the practical difference? To recite the Shema"—which is difficult: why ask "what is the practical difference," since previously it offered no halakhic difference, and it should simply have said: "The sign is for one sleeping in a dark room"?
עַל כָּרְחֲךָ לָזֶה אֵין צָרִיךְ סִימָן, רַק הַסִּימָן הוּא שֶׁנִּיכָּר לְמַטָּה אֵיזֶה שִׁינּוּי אָז, וְזֶה לְאוֹת עַל הַשְּׁאָגָה.
Perforce, for the natural time itself one requires no sign, but the sign denotes a discernible terrestrial change occurring then, serving as a token of the divine Roar.
אֲבָל אַחַר כָּךְ "לְמַאן דְּגָנֵי" קָשֶׁה: לְמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ? הוּצְרַךְ לוֹמַר "לִמְקְרֵי קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע".
But afterward, regarding "one who is sleeping," the Gemara challenges: what practical difference does it make? and was obliged to answer: "To recite Shema."
וְהוּא הַדִּין דְּשָׁם הֲוָה מָצֵי לְמֵימַר לְיוֹם הַמְּעוּנָּן אוֹ זְרִיחַת אוֹר הַלְּבָנָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, אֶלָּא דְּמַאי דִּשְׁכִיחַ טְפֵי נָקַט:
And the same applies that the Talmud could just as well have mentioned an overcast day or misleading moonlight as noted above, but it cited the most common scenario: one sleeping in a dark room.

sections.en: One Who Sleeps in a Dark House"

p: כח] מַאן דְּגָנֵי בְּבַיִת אָפֵל.
"One who sleeps in a dark house"
פֵּירוּשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין צב.): "הֱוֵי קַבֵּל וְקַיֵּים, כִּדִתְנַן: בַּיִת אָפֵל וְכוּלֵי".
is explained according to Sanhedrin (92a): "Accept your lot and endure, as we learn: a dark house, etc."
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵין מֵאִיר בּוֹ שׁוּם אוֹר אֱלֹהוּת, וְלֹא יָדַע זְמַן קַבָּלַת עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם אֵימָתַי,
This allegorically depicts a person within whom no divine light shines, who does not perceive when the time to accept the yoke of Heaven arrives;
כֵּיוָן דְּשָׁמַע תִּינוֹק וְכוּלֵי יְצָרֵף עַצְמוֹ בַּהֲדֵי צִיבּוּרָא וּבַהֲדֵי רָאשֵׁי הָעֵדָה,
but once he hears the infant and the woman, let him attach himself to the congregation and to the leaders of the community,
וּבַהֲדַיְיהוּ גַּם הוּא יוּכַל לְקַבֵּל, כַּיָּדוּעַ כַּאֲשֶׁר נִכְלָל נַפְשׁוֹ בְּנִשְׁמַת גְּדוֹלֵי הַדּוֹר הֵם מַעֲלִים אוֹתוֹ.
and alongside them he too will become capable of accepting the yoke, for as is known, when a person binds his soul into the collective soul of the generation's leaders, they elevate him.
וְדַוְקָא כְּשֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לָצֵאת מִן הַבַּיִת אָפֵל, דְּלָא עָדִיף הַאי סִימָנָא מֵחֲזָקָה, דְּהֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא לְבָרוּרֵי מְבָרְרִינַן, וְיֵצֵא לַחוּץ לִרְאוֹת.
